matthew-1.summary: Matthew opens with the family line of Jesus Christ, son of David and Abraham. It runs in three sets of fourteen generations. Four women appear in it: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and Uriah’s wife. Mary is pledged to Joseph and is found with child by the Holy Spirit. Joseph plans to end the engagement quietly. An angel tells him in a dream to take Mary as his wife. The child will be named Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins. Joseph does as he is told.

verse.text: Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

matthew-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-2.summary: Wise men from the east come to Jerusalem seeking the newborn king of the Jews. King Herod is troubled and learns the Christ should be born in Bethlehem. The star leads the wise men to the child, and they worship him with gifts. A dream warns them not to return to Herod. An angel tells Joseph to flee to Egypt with the child and his mother. Herod kills the young boys of Bethlehem. After Herod dies, Joseph brings the family back. They settle in Nazareth in Galilee.

verse.text: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.”

routes.title: The wise men go to Bethlehem
routes.text: Wise men from the east ask in Jerusalem for the newborn king. Herod sends them on to Bethlehem.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Flight into Egypt
routes.text: An angel warns Joseph in a dream. He takes the child and his mother to Egypt by night.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Return to Nazareth
routes.text: After Herod dies, Joseph brings the family back. He fears Archelaus in Judea and settles in Nazareth.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-3.summary: John the Baptist preaches in the desert of Judea. He tells people to repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is near. He wears camel’s hair and eats locusts and wild honey. Crowds come and are baptized in the Jordan, confessing their sins. He warns the Pharisees and Sadducees to bear fruit that fits repentance. They must not rely on having Abraham as their father. Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized. The Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice calls him God’s beloved Son.

verse.text: Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance!

routes.title: Jesus comes to the Jordan
routes.text: Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan, and John baptizes him.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-4.summary: The Spirit leads Jesus into the desert, where he fasts forty days. The devil tells him to turn stones into bread. He tells him to throw himself from the temple and trust the angels. He offers all the world’s kingdoms in return for worship. Jesus answers each time from Deuteronomy. He then begins to preach in Galilee. He calls four fishermen, who leave their nets and follow him. He heals the sick, and great crowds gather.

verse.text: Jesus said to him, “Again, it is written, ‘You shall not test the Lord, your God.’ ”

routes.title: Jesus moves to Capernaum
routes.text: Jesus hears that John is in prison. He leaves Nazareth and lives in Capernaum by the sea.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-5.summary: Jesus goes up a mountain and teaches his disciples. He calls the poor in spirit, the mourners, and the merciful blessed. His followers are salt and light. He has come to fulfill the law, not to destroy it. Anger and insult are judged along with murder. He speaks about lust, divorce, oaths, and revenge. He tells them to love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them. They are to be complete, as their Father is.

verse.text: leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

matthew-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-8.summary: Jesus comes down from the mountain and heals a man with a skin disease. A Roman officer asks him to heal a paralyzed servant. The officer says Jesus need only speak the word. Jesus marvels at his faith and heals the servant. He heals Peter’s mother-in-law and many others. He warns would-be followers of the cost. He calms a storm on the lake. Across the water he frees two men from demons, and the town sends him away.

verse.text: For I am also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

matthew-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-11.summary: John the Baptist is in prison and hears what Jesus is doing. He sends disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come. Jesus tells them to report what they see and hear. He praises John as more than a prophet. He says this generation is like children who are never satisfied. He rebukes towns that saw his works and did not repent. He thanks the Father for showing these things to little children. He invites the weary to come and find rest.

verse.text: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.

matthew-11.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-15.summary: Pharisees ask why the disciples do not wash their hands before eating. Jesus says they set aside God’s command for their tradition. What comes out of the mouth defiles a person, not what goes in. He travels to the region of Tyre and Sidon. A Canaanite woman begs him to heal her daughter. He says he was sent to Israel, and she keeps asking. He praises her faith and heals the girl. Back in Galilee he heals many and feeds four thousand.

verse.text: But she said, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”

routes.title: Jesus withdraws toward Tyre and Sidon
routes.text: Jesus withdraws into the region of Tyre and Sidon. A Canaanite woman meets him there.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-15.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-16.summary: Pharisees and Sadducees ask Jesus for a sign from heaven. He warns his disciples about their teaching. He asks the disciples who they say he is. Peter answers that he is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus blesses him and speaks of building his assembly. Then he says he must suffer, be killed, and rise. Peter rebukes him, and Jesus calls him a stumbling block. Anyone who follows him must take up a cross.

verse.text: But he turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.”

routes.title: Jesus goes toward Caesarea Philippi
routes.text: Jesus comes into the parts of Caesarea Philippi. He asks the disciples who people say he is.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-16.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-17.summary: Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. His face shines like the sun, and Moses and Elijah appear with him. Peter offers to build three shelters. A bright cloud covers them, and a voice calls Jesus the beloved Son. The disciples fall down afraid, and Jesus touches them. He tells them to say nothing until he has risen. Below, he heals a boy the disciples could not heal. He again says he will be killed and raised.

verse.text: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. Behold, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”

matthew-17.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-19.summary: Pharisees test Jesus with a question about divorce. He points them to the beginning, when God joined man and woman. People bring children, and he blesses them. A rich young man asks what good thing he must do to have eternal life. He says he has kept the commandments. Jesus tells him to sell what he has and give to the poor. The young man goes away sad. Jesus says the last will be first.

verse.text: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

routes.title: Jesus leaves Galilee
routes.text: Jesus departs from Galilee. He comes into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-19.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-20.summary: Jesus tells of a landowner who hires workers at dawn for a day’s wage. He hires more at later hours, even an hour before sunset. At evening each receives the same wage. Those hired first complain. Jesus again foretells his death and resurrection. The mother of James and John asks for the best seats for her sons. Jesus says the great must be servants. He gives sight to two blind men near Jericho.

verse.text: saying, ‘These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’

routes.title: Up from Jericho toward Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus goes up toward Jerusalem with the twelve. A great crowd follows him out of Jericho.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-21.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey, and crowds shout “Hosanna.” He drives the traders out of the temple and heals there. The chief priests ask by what authority he acts. He answers with a question about John’s baptism. He tells of two sons, only one of whom obeys. He tells of tenants who kill the owner’s servants and then his son. He says the Kingdom will be given to others. The leaders want to arrest him and fear the crowds.

verse.text: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spoke about them.

routes.title: Jesus enters Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus rides down from the Mount of Olives into Jerusalem. That evening he goes out to Bethany.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-23.summary: Jesus speaks to the crowds and his disciples about the scribes and Pharisees. They teach the law and do not practice it. They load others with heavy burdens and love titles and honor. He pronounces a series of woes on them. They shut the Kingdom against people. They tithe small herbs and neglect justice, mercy, and faith. They are like whitewashed tombs. He grieves over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets.

verse.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.

matthew-23.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-24.summary: Jesus says the temple’s stones will all be thrown down. On the Mount of Olives his disciples ask when and what the sign will be. He warns of false christs, wars, famines, and persecution. They must flee when they see the desolating sacrilege. The Son of Man will come like lightning. No one knows the day or hour, not even the angels. As in Noah’s days, people will be caught unaware. So they must watch and be ready.

verse.text: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has set over his household, to give them their food in due season?

matthew-24.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.
matthew-24.relatedNote: Jesus foretells the temple's fall in Matthew 24:2. Rome destroyed it in 70 CE.

matthew-26.summary: The chief priests plot to kill Jesus, and a woman anoints him with costly oil. Judas agrees to hand him over for thirty pieces of silver. Jesus eats the Passover with the twelve and gives them bread and the cup. Peter promises never to deny him. In Gethsemane Jesus prays while the disciples sleep. Judas arrives with an armed crowd, and Jesus is arrested. The council condemns him for blasphemy. Peter denies knowing him three times and weeps.

verse.text: Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.

routes.title: From Bethany to the Mount of Olives
routes.text: Jesus is at Bethany, then keeps the Passover in the city. After the hymn they go out to the Mount of Olives.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

matthew-26.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-27.summary: Jesus is handed to Pilate, the governor. Judas returns the silver and hangs himself. Pilate questions Jesus and offers to release a prisoner. The crowd asks for Barabbas. Pilate washes his hands and says he is innocent of this blood. Soldiers mock Jesus with a robe, a crown of thorns, and a reed. He is crucified between two robbers and dies. Joseph of Arimathea buries him, and the tomb is sealed and guarded.

verse.text: Then he released Barabbas to them, but Jesus he flogged and delivered to be crucified.

matthew-27.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

matthew-28.summary: At dawn after the Sabbath two women come to the tomb. An angel rolls back the stone and tells them Jesus has risen. They run to tell the disciples and meet Jesus on the way. The guards are paid to say the body was stolen. The eleven go to a mountain in Galilee. They worship him, though some doubt. He says all authority has been given to him. He sends them to make disciples of all nations and promises to be with them.

verse.text: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

routes.title: The eleven go to Galilee
routes.text: The angel says the risen Jesus goes ahead into Galilee. The eleven go to the mountain there.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

mark-1.summary: Mark begins with John the Baptist preaching in the desert. Jesus is baptized, and a voice from heaven calls him the beloved Son. He is tested in the desert for forty days. He announces that God’s Kingdom is near and calls four fishermen. In Capernaum he teaches with authority and drives out an unclean spirit. He heals Simon’s mother-in-law and many others at the door. Before dawn he goes out alone to pray. He then leaves for other towns and heals a man with a skin disease.

verse.text: He said to them, “Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”

routes.title: From Nazareth to the Jordan and Capernaum
routes.text: Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptized in the Jordan. He then goes into Galilee and enters Capernaum.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

mark-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-2.summary: Four men carry a paralyzed man to Jesus and lower him through the roof. Jesus forgives his sins and heals him. He calls Levi the tax collector and eats with sinners. He is asked why his disciples do not fast. He says no one puts new wine into old wineskins. On a Sabbath his disciples pick grain as they walk. Pharisees object, and he recalls what David did when hungry. He says the Sabbath was made for people.

verse.text: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.

mark-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-3.summary: Jesus enters a synagogue where a man has a withered hand. His opponents watch to see whether he will heal on the Sabbath. He asks whether the Sabbath is for doing good or harm, saving life or killing. They say nothing, and he heals the man. The Pharisees begin to plot his death. Crowds press on him, and he appoints twelve to be with him. Scribes say he drives out demons by their ruler. He says those who do God’s will are his family.

verse.text: He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good or to do harm? To save a life or to kill?” But they were silent.

mark-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-4.summary: Jesus teaches a large crowd from a boat. A farmer sows seed on path, rock, thorns, and good soil. He explains the story to his disciples in private. A lamp is meant to be set on a stand. Seed grows by itself while the farmer sleeps. The Kingdom is like a tiny mustard seed that becomes a large plant. That evening a storm fills the boat while Jesus sleeps. He rebukes the wind, and the disciples are terrified.

verse.text: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and asked him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”

mark-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-5.summary: Jesus crosses the lake and frees a man held by many demons. The man had lived among tombs, and no chain could hold him. The townspeople beg Jesus to leave. Jairus, a synagogue leader, begs him to come to his dying daughter. On the way a woman who has bled for twelve years touches his cloak. She is healed, and Jesus stops to find her. Word comes that the girl has died. Jesus takes her hand, and she gets up.

verse.text: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”

mark-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-6.summary: Jesus teaches in his home town, and the people take offense. He sends the twelve out two by two. Herod has John the Baptist beheaded after a rash promise at a feast. The twelve return, and Jesus takes them aside to rest. A crowd follows, and he feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish. That night he walks on the sea toward the disciples’ boat. They are terrified, and he gets in with them. People bring the sick wherever he goes.

verse.text: for they hadn’t understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.

mark-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-7.summary: Pharisees ask why Jesus’s disciples eat with unwashed hands. He says they honor God with their lips and hold to human tradition. The law says to honor father and mother. They let a man declare his goods “Corban,” a gift to God. He then gives his parents nothing. Jesus says evil comes from within, out of the heart. He heals a foreign woman’s daughter. He opens the ears and mouth of a deaf man.

verse.text: “then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,

routes.title: Through Tyre and Sidon to the lake
routes.text: Jesus goes to the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He comes back to the Sea of Galilee through the Decapolis.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

mark-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-8.summary: Jesus feeds four thousand people with seven loaves. Pharisees ask for a sign, and he refuses. In the boat the disciples worry that they have one loaf. He asks whether they still do not understand. At Bethsaida he heals a blind man in two stages. He asks who they say he is, and Peter calls him the Christ. Jesus says he must suffer, and Peter rebukes him. Jesus says his followers must take up their cross.

verse.text: He looked up, and said, “I see men, but I see them like walking trees.”

routes.title: From Bethsaida toward Caesarea Philippi
routes.text: Jesus heals a blind man at Bethsaida. He then goes to the villages of Caesarea Philippi.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

mark-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-9.summary: Jesus is changed in appearance on a mountain before three disciples. A voice from the cloud tells them to listen to him. Below, a father has brought a son whom the disciples could not heal. The father asks Jesus to help if he can. Jesus says all things are possible for one who believes. The father cries that he believes and asks help for his unbelief. Jesus heals the boy and again foretells his death. The disciples argue about who is greatest.

verse.text: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”

mark-9.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-10.summary: Jesus teaches about marriage and blesses the children. A rich man asks how to inherit eternal life and leaves in sorrow. Jesus foretells his death a third time. James and John ask to sit at his right and left in glory. He says whoever would be great must be a servant. At Jericho a blind beggar named Bartimaeus cries out to him. Jesus asks what he wants. He asks to see, receives his sight, and follows Jesus.

verse.text: Jesus asked him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”

routes.title: Beyond the Jordan to Jericho
routes.text: Jesus teaches beyond the Jordan, then goes up toward Jerusalem. He heals Bartimaeus as he leaves Jericho.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

mark-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-11.summary: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a colt, and people shout “Hosanna.” The next day he finds a fig tree with leaves and no fruit. He says no one will eat from it again. He drives the buyers and sellers out of the temple. He says God’s house should be a house of prayer for all nations. The following morning the fig tree has withered. He teaches about faith, prayer, and forgiveness. The leaders ask by what authority he does these things.

verse.text: He taught, saying to them, “Isn’t it written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers!”

routes.title: Jesus enters Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus rides from the Mount of Olives into Jerusalem. He looks around the temple and goes out to Bethany.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

mark-11.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-12.summary: Jesus tells of tenants who kill a vineyard owner’s son. He is asked about paying taxes to Caesar and about the resurrection. A scribe asks which commandment is first. Jesus names love of God and love of neighbor. He warns about scribes who love honor and devour widows’ houses. He sits and watches people put money in the temple treasury. Rich people give large sums. A poor widow gives two small coins, all she has.

verse.text: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”

mark-12.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-13.summary: A disciple admires the temple’s great stones. Jesus says not one will be left on another. Four disciples ask when this will happen. He warns of deceivers, wars, earthquakes, and trials before councils. They must flee when they see the desolating sacrilege. The Son of Man will come in the clouds. No one knows the day or the hour. They must stay awake, like servants whose master is away.

verse.text: “But of that day or that hour no one knows—not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

mark-13.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-14.summary: The leaders look for a way to arrest Jesus. At Bethany a woman pours costly perfume on his head. Some scold her, and Jesus defends her. Judas agrees to betray him. Jesus eats the Passover and gives the bread and the cup. In Gethsemane he prays in anguish while his friends sleep. He is arrested, and all the disciples run. The council condemns him, and Peter denies him three times.

verse.text: She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying.

routes.title: From Bethany to the Mount of Olives
routes.text: A woman anoints Jesus at Bethany. He keeps the Passover in the city and goes out to the Mount of Olives.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

mark-14.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-15.summary: The council hands Jesus to Pilate. Pilate offers to release him, and the crowd chooses Barabbas. Soldiers dress Jesus in purple and mock him as king. Simon of Cyrene is made to carry his cross. He is crucified with two robbers, and passersby mock him. Darkness covers the land, and he cries out and dies. The temple curtain tears in two. A Roman officer says this man was the Son of God.

verse.text: When the centurion, who stood by opposite him, saw that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”

mark-15.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

mark-16.summary: After the Sabbath three women bring spices to the tomb. They wonder who will roll away the stone. They find it moved and a young man in white inside. He says Jesus has risen and is not there. They must tell his disciples and Peter that he goes ahead to Galilee. The women flee, trembling and afraid. The longer ending tells of Jesus appearing to Mary Magdalene and others. He sends the eleven into all the world.

verse.text: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, as he said to you.’ ”

routes.text: The young man at the tomb says Jesus goes ahead into Galilee. The disciples will see him there.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

luke-1.summary: Luke says he has written an orderly account from eyewitness reports. An angel tells the old priest Zacharias that his wife will bear a son, John. Zacharias doubts and is made unable to speak. Gabriel tells Mary she will bear a son called the Son of the Most High. Mary visits Elizabeth, who blesses her. Mary sings that God has looked on her low position. John is born, and Zacharias speaks again. He praises God for raising up a savior.

verse.text: He has filled the hungry with good things. He has sent the rich away empty.

luke-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-2.summary: Caesar Augustus orders a registration, and Joseph and Mary travel to Bethlehem. Mary gives birth and lays her son in a feeding trough. Angels announce the birth to shepherds in the fields. The shepherds find the child and tell what they heard. In the temple old Simeon takes the child in his arms. He calls him a light for the nations and warns Mary of sorrow. The prophetess Anna gives thanks. At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the temple among the teachers.

verse.text: Yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”

routes.title: Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem
routes.text: Joseph goes up from Nazareth to Bethlehem to be enrolled. Mary goes with him.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: To the temple and home
routes.text: They bring the child to Jerusalem to present him. Then they return to Nazareth.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The Passover trip at age twelve
routes.text: His parents go up to Jerusalem for the Passover. The boy stays behind in the temple, then goes home with them.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

luke-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.
luke-2.relatedNote: Luke 2:1 names the decree of Caesar Augustus that sent Joseph to Bethlehem.

luke-3.summary: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius, John preaches a baptism of repentance. He warns the crowds not to rely on descent from Abraham. The people ask what they should do. He tells them to share coats and food. Tax collectors must collect no more than is due. Soldiers must not extort money. John says one mightier than he is coming. Jesus is baptized, and Luke traces his family line back to Adam.

verse.text: He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”

luke-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-4.summary: Jesus is tested by the devil in the desert for forty days. He returns to Galilee and teaches in the synagogues. In Nazareth he reads from Isaiah about good news for the poor. He says the Scripture is fulfilled that day. The people speak well of him at first. He reminds them that Elijah helped a foreign widow and Elisha a Syrian. They are furious and try to throw him off a cliff. He goes on to Capernaum and heals many.

verse.text: Elijah was sent to none of them, except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.

routes.title: From the Jordan to Nazareth and Capernaum
routes.text: Jesus returns from the Jordan and is tested in the wilderness. He reads in Nazareth and then goes down to Capernaum.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

luke-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-5.summary: Jesus teaches from Simon’s boat and tells him to let down the nets. They catch so many fish that the nets begin to break. Simon, James, and John leave everything and follow him. He heals a man with a skin disease and a paralyzed man. He calls Levi, a tax collector, who leaves his booth. Levi gives a great feast with many tax collectors. Pharisees complain about the company. Jesus says he came to call sinners to repentance.

verse.text: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”

luke-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-6.summary: Jesus is challenged twice about the Sabbath. He spends a night in prayer and chooses twelve apostles. He teaches a great crowd on level ground. He blesses the poor and the hungry and warns the rich. He tells them to love their enemies and do good to those who hate them. They should lend and expect nothing back. They should not judge, and they should forgive. The one who hears and acts builds on rock.

verse.text: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.

luke-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-7.summary: Jesus heals a Roman officer’s servant from a distance. At Nain he raises a widow’s only son. John the Baptist sends to ask whether Jesus is the one to come. A Pharisee named Simon invites Jesus to dinner. A woman known as a sinner weeps over his feet and anoints them. Simon thinks a prophet would know what she is. Jesus tells of two debtors forgiven different amounts. He tells the woman that her sins are forgiven.

verse.text: Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head.

luke-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-8.summary: Jesus travels with the twelve and with women who support them from their own means. He tells of a farmer sowing seed on four soils. His mother and brothers cannot reach him through the crowd. He says his family are those who hear God’s word and do it. He calms a storm on the lake. He frees a man from many demons. A woman with long bleeding is healed. He raises the daughter of Jairus.

verse.text: But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”

luke-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-9.summary: Jesus sends the twelve to preach and heal, and he feeds five thousand. Peter says he is the Christ of God. Jesus says he must suffer and that followers must take up their cross daily. He is changed in appearance on a mountain. The disciples argue over who is greatest. Jesus sets his face to go to Jerusalem. A Samaritan village refuses him. James and John want to call down fire, and he rebukes them.

verse.text: But he turned and rebuked them, “You don’t know of what kind of spirit you are.

routes.title: Jesus sets out for Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus sets his face to go to Jerusalem. The following chapters stay on this journey.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

luke-9.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-10.summary: Jesus sends seventy others ahead of him in pairs. They return with joy at what they have done. A lawyer asks what he must do to inherit eternal life. He agrees that the law says to love God and neighbor. He then asks who his neighbor is. Jesus tells of a man beaten by robbers and left half dead. A priest and a Levite pass by, and a Samaritan cares for him. Jesus then visits Martha and Mary.

verse.text: Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”

routes.title: The road in the parable
routes.intro: A lawyer asks Jesus who his neighbor is. Jesus answers with the parable of the good Samaritan.
routes.text: A man goes down from Jerusalem to Jericho and falls among robbers.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

luke-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-13.summary: People tell Jesus about Galileans whom Pilate killed. He asks whether they were worse sinners than others. He says no, and that everyone must repent. He tells of a fig tree given one more year. On a Sabbath he heals a woman bent over for eighteen years. The synagogue ruler objects. Jesus says she is a daughter of Abraham and should be set free. He weeps over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets.

verse.text: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”

luke-13.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-17.summary: Jesus warns against causing others to stumble and tells his disciples to forgive. A servant does not expect thanks for doing his duty. Between Samaria and Galilee ten men with a skin disease cry out for mercy. Jesus tells them to show themselves to the priests. They are healed as they go. One returns, praises God, and thanks Jesus, and he is a Samaritan. The Pharisees ask when God’s Kingdom will come. Jesus says it will come like lightning.

verse.text: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this foreigner?”

luke-17.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-18.summary: Jesus tells of a widow who keeps asking an unjust judge for justice. He tells of two men who pray in the temple. A Pharisee thanks God that he is not like other people. A tax collector asks only for mercy. People bring infants, and Jesus welcomes them. A rich ruler asks about eternal life and leaves sad. Jesus foretells his death again. Near Jericho he gives sight to a blind beggar.

verse.text: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’

luke-18.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-19.summary: In Jericho a rich tax collector named Zacchaeus climbs a tree to see Jesus. Jesus stays at his house, and Zacchaeus promises to repay those he cheated. Jesus tells of servants entrusted with money while their master is away. He rides a colt toward Jerusalem. The disciples praise God loudly. As the city comes into view, he weeps over it. He says it did not know what would bring peace. He drives the sellers from the temple and teaches there daily.

verse.text: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it,

routes.title: From Jericho up to Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus passes through Jericho and meets Zacchaeus. He goes up by Bethany and the Mount of Olives and weeps over the city.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

luke-19.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-20.summary: The chief priests and scribes ask Jesus by what authority he acts. He asks them about John’s baptism, and they will not answer. He tells of tenants who beat the owner’s servants and kill his son. The leaders know the story is about them. They send spies to trap him with a question about taxes. Sadducees ask about the resurrection. He asks how the Christ can be David’s son. He warns the people about scribes who devour widows’ houses.

verse.text: The chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour, but they feared the people—for they knew he had spoken this parable against them.

luke-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-21.summary: Jesus sees a poor widow put two small coins in the treasury. Some admire the temple’s fine stones and gifts. He says not one stone will be left on another. They ask when and what the sign will be. He warns them not to follow those who say the time is near. Wars and disturbances must come, and the end is not yet. Jerusalem will be surrounded by armies. He tells them to stay alert and pray.

verse.text: When you hear of wars and disturbances, don’t be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end won’t come immediately.”

luke-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-22.summary: Judas agrees with the chief priests to hand Jesus over. Jesus eats the Passover with the apostles and gives the bread and the cup. He says one at the table will betray him. The apostles then argue about who is greatest. He says he is among them as one who serves. He prays on the Mount of Olives in anguish. He is arrested, and Peter denies him three times. The council asks whether he is the Son of God.

verse.text: For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.

luke-22.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-23.summary: The council brings Jesus to Pilate and accuses him of stirring up the nation. Pilate finds no basis for a charge and sends him to Herod. Herod mocks him and sends him back. Pilate says three times that Jesus has done nothing deserving death. The crowd demands Barabbas. Pilate grants their demand. Jesus is crucified and prays for those who do it. One criminal asks to be remembered, and Jesus dies.

verse.text: Pilate decreed that what they asked for should be done.

luke-23.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

luke-24.summary: Women find the tomb empty, and two men in shining clothes say Jesus has risen. The apostles think their report is nonsense. Two disciples walk to Emmaus, and a stranger joins them. They tell him their hopes have been crushed. He explains the Scriptures about the Christ. At supper he breaks bread, and they know him. He appears to the group in Jerusalem and eats fish. He blesses them and is carried up to heaven.

verse.text: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”

routes.title: Jesus leads them out to Bethany
routes.text: Jesus leads the disciples out as far as Bethany and blesses them.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

luke-24.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-1.summary: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God and was God. All things were made through him. The Word became flesh and lived among us. John the Baptist says he is not the Christ. He points to Jesus as the Lamb of God. Two of John’s disciples follow Jesus and spend the day with him. Andrew brings his brother Simon. Philip brings Nathanael, who doubts that anything good comes from Nazareth.

verse.text: He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.

routes.title: From the Jordan to Galilee
routes.text: John baptizes at Bethany beyond the Jordan. The next day Jesus decides to go into Galilee.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

john-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-2.summary: Jesus and his disciples attend a wedding at Cana. The wine runs out, and his mother tells him. He has six stone jars filled with water. The water becomes fine wine, and his disciples believe in him. He goes up to Jerusalem for the Passover. He drives the sellers and money changers out of the temple. He says, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” He was speaking about his body.

verse.text: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus had said.

routes.title: From Cana to Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus is at a wedding in Cana. He goes down to Capernaum and then up to Jerusalem for the Passover.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

john-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-3.summary: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler, comes to Jesus at night. Jesus says no one can see God’s Kingdom without being born anew. Nicodemus asks how that can be. Jesus says God loved the world and gave his only Son. Light has come, and people loved darkness. John’s disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus. John says he is the bridegroom’s friend and is glad. He says Jesus must increase and he must decrease.

verse.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

john-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-4.summary: Jesus travels through Samaria and rests at Jacob’s well. He asks a Samaritan woman for a drink. He offers her living water and tells her about her life. She asks where people ought to worship. He says true worshipers worship in spirit and truth. She tells her town to come and see. Many Samaritans believe and ask him to stay. In Galilee he heals an official’s son with a word.

verse.text: They said to the woman, “Now we believe, not because of your speaking; for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.”

routes.title: Through Samaria to Galilee
routes.text: Jesus leaves Judea and passes through Samaria. He stops at Sychar and comes again to Cana. Jerusalem stands for Judea here.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

john-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-5.summary: In Jerusalem many sick people lie beside a pool. One man has been ill for thirty-eight years. Jesus asks whether he wants to be well. The man says he has no one to put him in the water. Jesus tells him to take up his mat and walk. It is the Sabbath, and the leaders object. Jesus says his Father is working and he is working. He says the Scriptures testify about him.

verse.text: The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.”

routes.title: Up to Jerusalem for a feast
routes.text: Jesus goes up to Jerusalem for a feast of the Jews.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

john-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-6.summary: Jesus feeds five thousand with five barley loaves and two fish. The crowd wants to make him king, and he withdraws. He walks on the sea to his disciples. The crowd finds him and asks for more bread. He says he is the bread of life that came down from heaven. He speaks of eating his flesh and drinking his blood. Many disciples call this a hard saying and leave. Peter says there is no one else to go to.

verse.text: Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.

john-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-7.summary: Jesus’s brothers urge him to show himself at the Feast of Booths. He goes up in secret and then teaches in the temple. Some say he is a good man, and others say he deceives the people. Officers are sent to arrest him. On the last day he invites the thirsty to come and drink. The crowd is divided over him. The officers return without him and say no one ever spoke like this. Nicodemus asks whether the law judges a man unheard.

verse.text: “Does our law judge a man unless it first hears from him personally and knows what he does?”

routes.title: Up to the feast in secret
routes.text: Jesus stays in Galilee while his brothers go up. Then he goes up to the feast in secret.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

john-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-8.summary: Jesus says he is the light of the world. The Pharisees say his witness about himself is not valid. He tells those who believed him that the truth will set them free. They answer that they are Abraham’s children and were never slaves. He says everyone who sins is a slave to sin. If they were Abraham’s children, they would do what Abraham did. They are trying to kill him. He says, “Before Abraham came into existence, I AM.”

verse.text: But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do this.

john-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-9.summary: Jesus sees a man blind from birth. The disciples ask whose sin caused it. He says neither, and he heals the man with mud and washing. Neighbors and Pharisees question the man again and again. His parents are afraid and say he can speak for himself. He says he knows one thing: he was blind and now sees. They throw him out. Jesus finds him, and the man worships him.

verse.text: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”

john-9.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-10.summary: Jesus says the shepherd enters by the door and the sheep know his voice. A thief comes only to steal and kill. Jesus says he is the door and the good shepherd. A hired man runs when the wolf comes. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. He has other sheep that are not of this fold. At a winter feast some ask whether he is the Christ. He says, “I and the Father are one,” and they pick up stones.

verse.text: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

routes.title: Jesus goes beyond the Jordan
routes.text: Jesus goes away beyond the Jordan to the place where John first baptized.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

john-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-11.summary: Lazarus of Bethany falls ill, and his sisters send for Jesus. Jesus arrives after Lazarus has been dead four days. Martha says she believes he is the Christ. Jesus weeps at the tomb. He calls Lazarus out, and the dead man comes out wrapped in cloths. Many believe, and some report it to the Pharisees. The council fears that Rome will destroy their place and nation. The high priest says one man should die for the people.

verse.text: nor do you consider that it is advantageous for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation not perish.”

routes.title: Jesus comes to Bethany
routes.text: Jesus waits two days after he hears Lazarus is sick. Then he goes to Bethany, near Jerusalem.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

john-11.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-12.summary: Mary anoints Jesus’s feet with costly perfume, and Judas objects. A crowd welcomes Jesus to Jerusalem with palm branches. Some Greeks ask to see him. He says the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. A grain of wheat must fall into the earth and die to bear fruit. A voice from heaven answers him. He says that when he is lifted up he will draw all people to himself. Many still do not believe.

verse.text: Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.

routes.title: From Bethany into Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus comes to Bethany six days before the Passover. The next day a crowd meets him as he comes to Jerusalem.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

john-12.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-18.summary: Jesus goes to a garden across the Kidron, and Judas brings soldiers. Jesus steps forward and says, “I am he.” Peter cuts off a servant’s ear, and Jesus tells him to put away his sword. Jesus is taken to the high priest. Peter denies him three times by a fire. Jesus tells the high priest that he taught openly. He is brought to Pilate, who asks whether he is a king. Jesus says his Kingdom is not of this world.

verse.text: Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is not of this world. If my Kingdom were of this world, then my servants would fight, that I wouldn’t be delivered to the Jews. But now my Kingdom is not from here.”

john-18.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-19.summary: Pilate has Jesus flogged, and soldiers crown him with thorns. Pilate says he finds no guilt and brings him out to the crowd. He hands him over to be crucified. The sign on the cross reads “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews.” Soldiers divide his clothes. Jesus entrusts his mother to the disciple he loves. He says, “It is finished,” and dies. Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus bury him in a garden tomb.

verse.text: Then he said to the disciple, “Behold, your mother!” From that hour, the disciple took her to his own home.

john-19.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-20.summary: Mary Magdalene finds the tomb open and runs to Peter and another disciple. They see the grave cloths and go home. Mary stays weeping and meets Jesus, whom she takes for the gardener. He says her name, and she knows him. That evening he appears to the disciples behind locked doors. Thomas is absent and says he will not believe without touching the wounds. A week later Jesus invites him to touch. John says he wrote so that readers may believe.

verse.text: but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.

john-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

john-21.summary: Seven disciples go fishing on the Sea of Tiberias and catch nothing. At dawn a man on the shore tells them to cast on the right side. The net fills, and they know it is the Lord. He gives them bread and fish beside a charcoal fire. He asks Peter three times whether he loves him. Each time he tells him to feed his sheep. Peter asks what will happen to another disciple. Jesus says that is not Peter’s concern.

verse.text: This saying therefore went out among the brothers that this disciple wouldn’t die. Yet Jesus didn’t say to him that he wouldn’t die, but, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?”

john-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

acts-1.summary: The writer opens a second book for Theophilus. The risen Jesus teaches the apostles for forty days. He tells them to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Spirit. They ask if he will now restore the kingdom to Israel. He is taken up, and two men in white speak to them. About 120 believers pray together in an upper room. Peter says another witness must take the place of Judas. They pray and cast lots, and the lot falls on Matthias.

verse.text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”

acts-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

acts-2.summary: On the day of Pentecost a sound like wind fills the house. Tongues like fire rest on the believers, and they speak in other languages. Jews from many nations hear their own languages. Some are amazed, and others say the speakers are drunk. Peter quotes Joel and says God raised Jesus from the dead. The hearers ask what they should do. Peter tells them to repent and be baptized. About three thousand join, and they share teaching, meals, prayer, and goods.

verse.text: For the promise is to you and to your children, and to all who are far off, even as many as the Lord our God will call to himself.”

acts-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

acts-3.summary: Peter and John go to the temple at the hour of prayer. A man lame from birth asks them for money at the gate. Peter says he has no silver or gold. He tells the man to walk in the name of Jesus Christ. The man leaps, walks, and praises God in the temple. A crowd runs together in Solomon’s porch. Peter says God raised Jesus, whom they had denied. He says they acted in ignorance and calls them to repent.

verse.text: When Peter saw it, he responded to the people, “You men of Israel, why do you marvel at this man? Why do you fasten your eyes on us, as though by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?

acts-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

acts-4.summary: The priests, the temple captain, and the Sadducees arrest Peter and John. The next day the rulers ask by what name they acted. Peter says the man stands healed by the name of Jesus. The council sees their boldness and notes they are untrained men. It orders them not to speak in Jesus’ name. Peter and John say they cannot stop telling what they saw. The believers pray for boldness, and the place shakes. They share goods, and Barnabas sells a field for those in need.

verse.text: for we can’t help telling the things which we saw and heard.”

acts-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

acts-5.summary: Ananias and Sapphira sell land and keep part of the price. They bring the rest as if it were the whole. Peter says Ananias lied to God, and Ananias falls dead. Three hours later Sapphira repeats the lie and also dies. The apostles heal many in Solomon’s porch. The high priest and the Sadducees jail them, but an angel opens the doors. Before the council Peter says they must obey God rather than men. Gamaliel advises caution, and the apostles are beaten and released.

verse.text: While you kept it, didn’t it remain your own? After it was sold, wasn’t it in your power? How is it that you have conceived this thing in your heart? You haven’t lied to men, but to God.”

acts-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

acts-6.summary: The number of disciples grows. The Hellenists, Jewish believers who spoke Greek, complain against the Hebrews. Their widows are being missed in the daily serving. The twelve ask the group to choose seven men for this work. The group chooses Stephen, Philip, and five others, and the apostles lay hands on them. The word spreads, and many priests believe. Stephen works signs, and men from a synagogue argue with him. They bring false witnesses and take him before the council.

verse.text: Therefore, select from among you, brothers, seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.

acts-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

acts-7.summary: The high priest asks Stephen if the charges are true. Stephen answers with Israel’s history. God appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia and was with Joseph in Egypt. Moses was pushed away by his own people, yet God sent him. The fathers made a calf in the wilderness. They had the tabernacle, and Solomon built a house. Stephen says his hearers resist the Holy Spirit as their fathers did. They stone him, and he prays that the sin not be held against them.

verse.text: However, the Most High doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says,

acts-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

acts-8.summary: Saul approves of Stephen’s death, and a great persecution scatters the believers. Philip tells the people of Samaria about Christ, and many are baptized. Simon, who had amazed the city with sorcery, is baptized too. Peter and John come and lay hands on them, and they receive the Holy Spirit. Simon offers money for that power, and Peter rebukes him. An angel sends Philip to a desert road. An Ethiopian official is reading Isaiah in his chariot. Philip tells him about Jesus and baptizes him.

verse.text: He said, “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” He begged Philip to come up and sit with him.

routes.title: Philip goes to Samaria
routes.intro: Stephen has been stoned in Jerusalem, and Saul is leading a persecution of the church. Philip was one of the seven chosen to serve the believers.
routes.text: Persecution scatters the Jerusalem assembly. Philip goes down to the city of Samaria and proclaims the Christ.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The road from Jerusalem to Gaza
routes.intro: Philip, one of the seven, has been preaching in Samaria. The Ethiopian official, treasurer to his queen, is going home from worship in Jerusalem.
routes.text: An angel sends Philip to this road. He meets the Ethiopian official on it. Acts does not say where.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Philip from Azotus to Caesarea
routes.intro: Philip has just baptized the Ethiopian official on the Gaza road. Then the Spirit takes him away.
routes.text: Philip is found at Azotus. He preaches in the towns until he reaches Caesarea.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-9.summary: Saul travels to Damascus with letters to arrest followers of the Way. A light from the sky stops him, and a voice says it is Jesus. He is blind for three days. The Lord sends a disciple named Ananias to him. Ananias lays hands on Saul, and Saul sees and is baptized. Saul speaks of Jesus in the synagogues, and opponents plot to kill him. Barnabas brings him to the apostles in Jerusalem. Peter heals Aeneas in Lydda and raises Tabitha in Joppa.

verse.text: But Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he did to your saints at Jerusalem.

routes.title: Saul sets out for Damascus
routes.intro: Saul, a Pharisee, is arresting followers of Jesus. He sets out to bring any he finds in Damascus back to Jerusalem in chains.
routes.text: Saul sets out for Damascus with letters from the high priest. A light stops him near the city.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Saul escapes to Tarsus
routes.intro: Saul, now a believer, has been preaching in Damascus that Jesus is the Son of God. The Jews there plot to kill him.
routes.text: Disciples lower Saul over the Damascus wall in a basket. He goes to Jerusalem. The brothers then send him to Tarsus by Caesarea.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Peter from Lydda to Joppa
routes.text: Peter heals Aeneas at Lydda. Two men bring him to Joppa, where Tabitha has died.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-10.summary: Cornelius is a centurion in Caesarea who fears God and gives to the poor. An angel tells him to send for Peter in Joppa. Peter sees a sheet full of animals and hears a voice tell him to eat. He refuses, and the voice says not to call unclean what God cleansed. The Spirit tells him to go with the messengers. In Cornelius’s house Peter says God shows no favoritism. The Holy Spirit falls on the Gentile hearers while he speaks. Peter orders that they be baptized.

verse.text: “Can anyone forbid these people from being baptized with water? They have received the Holy Spirit just like us.”

routes.title: Cornelius sends for Peter
routes.intro: Cornelius is a Roman centurion at Caesarea, a Gentile who prays to God. An angel has told him to send for Peter.
routes.text: Cornelius sends two servants and a soldier to Joppa to fetch Peter.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Peter goes to Caesarea
routes.intro: In a vision God has taught Peter to call no one unclean. Messengers from Cornelius, a Gentile centurion, have come for him.
routes.text: Peter goes with them the next day. Some brothers from Joppa go too.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-11.summary: Believers in Jerusalem criticize Peter for eating with uncircumcised men. Peter tells them the vision, the Spirit’s order, and the angel’s message to Cornelius. He says the Spirit fell on that household as on them at the beginning. They fall silent and then glorify God. Scattered believers reach Antioch, and some speak to Greeks. Barnabas comes, and he brings Saul from Tarsus. The disciples are first called Christians in Antioch. They send famine relief to Judea by Barnabas and Saul.

verse.text: If then God gave to them the same gift as us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?”

routes.title: Barnabas is sent to Antioch
routes.text: The Jerusalem assembly hears that Greeks in Antioch believe. It sends Barnabas there.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Barnabas brings Saul from Tarsus
routes.text: Barnabas goes to Tarsus to look for Saul and brings him to Antioch.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Relief for Judea
routes.text: The disciples at Antioch send relief to the elders in Judea. Barnabas and Saul carry it. Jerusalem stands for Judea here.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-12.summary: King Herod kills James the brother of John with the sword. He arrests Peter during the days of unleavened bread. The assembly prays for Peter. At night an angel wakes him, the chains fall off, and the iron gate opens. Peter goes to the house of Mary, mother of John Mark. A servant named Rhoda hears his voice and runs in without opening the gate. Herod orders the guards put to death. Later he accepts praise as a god, and an angel strikes him.

verse.text: They said to her, “You are crazy!” But she insisted that it was so. They said, “It is his angel.”

acts-13.summary: The Holy Spirit tells the assembly at Antioch to set apart Barnabas and Saul. On Cyprus the sorcerer Elymas opposes them and is struck blind. The proconsul Sergius Paulus believes. In Antioch of Pisidia the synagogue rulers invite Paul to speak. He tells Israel’s history from Egypt to David and says God raised Jesus. The next Sabbath almost the whole city gathers. Some Jewish hearers contradict Paul, and he turns to the Gentiles. The two are driven out and go on to Iconium.

verse.text: Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly, and said, “It was necessary that God’s word should be spoken to you first. Since indeed you thrust it from yourselves, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.

routes.title: From Antioch to Cyprus and Pisidia
routes.intro: The church at Antioch is told by the Holy Spirit to set apart Barnabas and Saul. This is Paul's first mission.
routes.text: Barnabas and Saul sail to Cyprus and cross the island. They sail to Perga and go up to Antioch of Pisidia. Driven out, they go to Iconium.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-14.summary: In Iconium Paul and Barnabas speak in the synagogue, and the city divides. They flee a plan to stone them. In Lystra Paul heals a man who had never walked. The crowd calls them Jupiter and Mercury, and a priest brings oxen to sacrifice. The two tear their clothes and say they are only men. Opponents from Antioch and Iconium arrive, and the crowd stones Paul. He gets up and goes on to Derbe. They return through the cities, appoint elders, and report in Antioch.

verse.text: “Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of the same nature as you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;

routes.title: Flight to Lystra and Derbe
routes.text: Paul and Barnabas flee a plot at Iconium. Paul is stoned at Lystra, and they go on to Derbe.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Return to Antioch
routes.text: They go back through the same cities and appoint elders. They sail from Attalia to Antioch.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-15.summary: Men from Judea teach in Antioch that Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved. Paul and Barnabas dispute this and go to Jerusalem. The apostles and elders meet. Peter says God gave the Gentiles the Spirit and made no distinction. James quotes the prophets and proposes four things to avoid. They send a letter with Judas and Silas, and Antioch rejoices. Paul and Barnabas then disagree over John Mark and part ways. Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia.

verse.text: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us, to lay no greater burden on you than these necessary things:

routes.title: Up to Jerusalem about the dispute
routes.intro: Some teachers from Judea are telling Gentile converts in Antioch that they must be circumcised to be saved.
routes.text: Antioch sends Paul and Barnabas to the apostles and elders. They pass through Phoenicia and Samaria.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The letter goes to Antioch
routes.intro: The council at Jerusalem has decided that Gentile converts need not be circumcised. Its letter tells the churches so.
routes.text: Judas and Silas carry the council’s letter to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-16.summary: Paul takes Timothy with him from Lystra. A vision of a man from Macedonia calls Paul across the sea. In Philippi Lydia, a seller of purple, believes and hosts them. Paul orders a spirit out of a slave girl who told fortunes. Her owners lose their income and accuse Paul and Silas before the magistrates. The two are beaten and jailed, and an earthquake opens the doors at midnight. The jailer and his household are baptized. Paul says they are Romans, and the magistrates come and ask them to leave.

verse.text: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, “Don’t harm yourself, for we are all here!”

routes.title: From Lystra to Philippi
routes.intro: Paul and Silas set out on a second mission to visit the churches founded on the first.
routes.text: Paul meets Timothy at Lystra. They pass through Phrygia and Galatia to Troas. After the vision they sail to Macedonia.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-16.dateDetail: The Church chronology dates letters from these journeys to AD 50 and 55.

acts-17.summary: In Thessalonica Paul reasons from the Scriptures for three Sabbaths. Some believe, and opponents raise a mob against Jason’s house. In Beroea the hearers examine the Scriptures daily. In Athens Paul is troubled by the city’s idols. Epicurean and Stoic philosophers bring him to the Areopagus. He speaks of the God who made the world and needs nothing. He quotes their poets and says God will judge through a man he raised. Some mock, some want to hear more, and a few believe.

verse.text: For as I passed along and observed the objects of your worship, I also found an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What therefore you worship in ignorance, I announce to you.

routes.title: From Philippi to Athens
routes.intro: On Paul's second mission he and Silas preach in Macedonia. In each city, opponents stir up crowds against them.
routes.text: Paul and Silas go to Thessalonica, then to Beroea by night. Brothers take Paul to the sea and on to Athens.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-17.dateDetail: The Church chronology dates letters from these journeys to AD 50 and 55.

acts-18.summary: In Corinth Paul lives and works with Aquila and Priscilla, who are tentmakers. He reasons in the synagogue each Sabbath. When opposed, he moves next door to the house of Titius Justus. Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believes. The Lord tells Paul in a vision not to be afraid. The proconsul Gallio refuses to judge a dispute about Jewish law. Paul sails to Ephesus, Caesarea, and Antioch. In Ephesus Apollos teaches well but knows only John’s baptism.

verse.text: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside, and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

routes.title: Paul comes to Corinth
routes.intro: On his second mission Paul has preached in Macedonia and at Athens.
routes.text: Paul leaves Athens for Corinth and stays a year and six months.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From Corinth back to Antioch
routes.intro: Paul has spent a year and a half founding the church at Corinth. He heads home to Antioch, ending his second mission.
routes.text: Paul sails for Syria by Cenchreae and Ephesus. He lands at Caesarea, greets the assembly, and goes down to Antioch.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-18.dateDetail: The Church chronology dates letters from these journeys to AD 50 and 55.

acts-19.summary: In Ephesus Paul meets twelve disciples who know only John’s baptism. He baptizes them in Jesus’ name, and they receive the Holy Spirit. He teaches for two years in the school of Tyrannus. Seven sons of Sceva misuse Jesus’ name, and a possessed man beats them. Many burn their books of magic. Demetrius, a silversmith who makes shrines of Artemis, gathers the craftsmen. A crowd fills the theater and shouts for two hours. The town clerk sends them home and points to the courts.

verse.text: whom he gathered together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.

acts-19.dateDetail: The Church chronology dates letters from these journeys to AD 50 and 55.

acts-20.summary: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece and returns by way of Troas. There Paul speaks until midnight, and young Eutychus falls from a window. Paul embraces him, and he is brought in alive. At Miletus Paul calls the elders of Ephesus. He says he taught them openly and house to house. He expects chains in Jerusalem and says they will not see him again. He warns of wolves and tells them to guard the flock. They kneel, pray, and weep.

verse.text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”

routes.title: From Philippi to Miletus
routes.intro: Paul is ending his third mission. He is hurrying to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost with a gift for the poor saints there.
routes.text: The group sails from Philippi to Troas. Paul goes to Assos by land. The ship then passes the islands to Miletus.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-20.dateDetail: The Church chronology dates letters from these journeys to AD 50 and 55.

acts-21.summary: Paul sails to Tyre and then to Caesarea, where he stays with Philip. The prophet Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul’s belt. He says Paul will be bound in Jerusalem. Paul says he is ready to die there. James and the elders report a rumor that he teaches Jews to leave Moses. They ask him to join four men in a vow at the temple. Men from Asia see him there and stir up the crowd. Roman soldiers take him, and he asks to speak.

verse.text: For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

routes.title: From Miletus to Jerusalem
routes.intro: Paul is ending his third mission and going to Jerusalem with a gift for the poor saints, though he has been warned that chains await him.
routes.text: The ship passes Cos and Rhodes to Patara. A second ship crosses to Tyre. The group goes on by Ptolemais and Caesarea to Jerusalem.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-22.summary: Paul speaks to the crowd in Hebrew, and they grow quiet. He says he is a Jew, taught by Gamaliel, and once persecuted the Way. He tells of the light near Damascus and the voice of Jesus. Ananias, a devout man, told him he would be a witness. Later, praying in the temple, he was told to leave Jerusalem. When he says he was sent to the Gentiles, the crowd shouts for his death. The officer orders him flogged. Paul says he is a Roman citizen by birth, and they stop.

verse.text: “He said to me, ‘Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.’ ”

acts-23.summary: Paul tells the council he has lived in good conscience. The high priest Ananias orders him struck. Paul says he is a Pharisee, on trial for the hope of resurrection. Pharisees and Sadducees then argue, and the officer pulls him out. That night the Lord tells him he must testify in Rome. More than forty men vow not to eat until they kill him. Paul’s nephew reports the plot to the officer. Soldiers take Paul by night to the governor Felix in Caesarea.

verse.text: The following night, the Lord stood by him and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”

routes.title: Paul is taken to Caesarea
routes.intro: Paul was arrested at the temple in Jerusalem. More than forty men have sworn to kill him, so the Roman commander sends him to the governor, Felix.
routes.text: Soldiers take Paul to Antipatris by night. Horsemen bring him on to the governor at Caesarea.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-24.summary: The high priest Ananias and a speaker named Tertullus bring charges before Felix. Tertullus calls Paul a plague and a leader of the Nazarene sect. He says Paul tried to profane the temple. Paul answers that no one found him arguing or stirring a crowd. He says he worships the God of his fathers and hopes for a resurrection. Felix puts off the case until Lysias comes. He and his wife Drusilla hear Paul, and Felix becomes afraid. He keeps Paul two years and leaves him bound.

verse.text: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often and talked with him.

acts-25.summary: Festus replaces Felix, and the chief priests ask him to send Paul to Jerusalem. They plan an ambush on the road. Festus hears the case in Caesarea, and the charges are not proved. He asks if Paul will be tried in Jerusalem. Paul says he stands at Caesar’s court and appeals to Caesar. Festus agrees to send him. King Agrippa and Bernice visit, and Festus explains the case. He brings Paul before them the next day.

verse.text: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”

acts-26.summary: Paul speaks before King Agrippa, Bernice, and Festus. He says he lived as a Pharisee and now stands trial for Israel’s hope. He tells how he jailed the saints and voted for their deaths. He describes the light on the Damascus road and the voice of Jesus. He says he obeyed the vision and taught Jews and Gentiles to repent.
