Festus shouts that learning has made him mad. Paul asks Agrippa if he believes the prophets. Agrippa says Paul could have been freed if he had not appealed.

verse.text: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”

acts-27.summary: Paul sails for Italy under a centurion named Julius. At Fair Havens he warns that the voyage will bring loss. The centurion follows the pilot and the owner, and they sail on. A violent wind drives the ship for many days. Paul says an angel told him no life will be lost. On the fourteenth night the sailors try to leave in the boat. Paul urges all 276 people to eat. The ship breaks up on a shore, and everyone reaches land.

verse.text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”

routes.title: The voyage toward Italy
routes.intro: Paul is a prisoner. He has appealed to Caesar, so the governor, Festus, sends him to Rome under a centurion named Julius. Luke and Aristarchus sail with him, and at Myra they board a ship of Alexandria bound for Italy.
routes.text: The ship touches at Sidon and reaches Myra. A second ship leaves Fair Havens, and a storm drives it to Malta.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

acts-28.summary: The survivors land on Malta, and the islanders show them kindness. A viper bites Paul, and he shakes it off unharmed. He heals the father of Publius and others. After three months they sail to Italy, and believers meet Paul on the road. In Rome Paul lives under guard and calls the Jewish leaders. He explains his case and teaches them from morning to evening. Some believe, and some do not. Paul quotes Isaiah, and for two years he receives all who come.

verse.text: preaching God’s Kingdom and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.

routes.title: From Malta to Rome
routes.intro: Paul, a prisoner bound for trial before Caesar, was shipwrecked on Malta with everyone aboard. After three months the party sails on in another ship of Alexandria.
routes.text: Paul sails by Syracuse and Rhegium to Puteoli. Brothers meet him at the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns. This guide has no checked point for the Market of Appius.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

romans-1.summary: Paul opens a letter to the believers in Rome. He calls himself an apostle set apart for God’s good news about his Son. He thanks God that their faith is known in all the world. He has often planned to visit and has been prevented. He says he is not ashamed of the good news. It is God’s power to save the Jew first and also the Greek. God’s wrath, he says, falls on those who trade his glory for images. God gives them up to their desires, and Paul lists the wrongs that follow.

verse.text: that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.

romans-15.summary: Paul says the strong should bear the weaknesses of the weak. Christ did not please himself. Paul tells them to accept one another as Christ accepted them. He quotes four Scriptures about Gentiles praising God. He explains that he has taught from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum. He plans to visit Rome on his way to Spain. First he will carry a gift from Macedonia and Achaia to Jerusalem’s poor. He asks them to pray for his safety in Judea.

verse.text: Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.

routes.title: Paul’s plan: Jerusalem, then Rome
routes.text: Paul says he is going to Jerusalem with a gift for the saints. After that he plans to visit Rome on the way to Spain.
routes.note: The line joins the places Romans names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

1-corinthians-1.summary: Paul and Sosthenes write to the assembly of God at Corinth. Paul thanks God for their gifts of speech and knowledge. Then he begs them to agree, for Chloe’s people report quarrels. Some say they follow Paul, and others Apollos, Cephas, or Christ. Paul is glad he baptized only a few of them. He says the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing. Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek wisdom, but he announces Christ crucified. God chose the weak and lowly, so no one may boast.

verse.text: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized into the name of Paul?

1-corinthians-15.summary: Paul repeats the good news he delivered. Christ died for sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day. He appeared to Cephas, the twelve, five hundred others, James, and Paul. Some in Corinth say there is no resurrection of the dead. Paul says that if so, Christ was not raised and faith is empty. But Christ has been raised, the first fruit of those who sleep. The body is sown perishable and raised imperishable, like a seed. Death is swallowed up, so their labor is not in vain.

verse.text: But now Christ has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruit of those who are asleep.

1-corinthians-16.summary: Paul gives directions for the collection for the saints. Each should set money aside on the first day of the week. Approved people will carry the gift to Jerusalem. Paul plans to come through Macedonia and stay in Ephesus until Pentecost. He asks them to receive Timothy without fear and says Apollos will come later. He tells them to watch, stand firm, and do everything in love. He commends the household of Stephanas. He signs the greeting with his own hand.

verse.text: Let all that you do be done in love.

routes.title: Paul’s plan to come to Corinth
routes.text: Paul will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost. Then he will pass through Macedonia and come to Corinth.
routes.note: The line joins the places 1 Corinthians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The gift for Jerusalem
routes.text: Paul will send approved people with letters to carry the gift to Jerusalem. He may go with them.
routes.note: The line joins the places 1 Corinthians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

2-corinthians-1.summary: Paul and Timothy write to the assembly at Corinth and the saints in Achaia. Paul blesses God, who comforts them in every affliction. That comfort lets them comfort others. In Asia they were burdened beyond their strength and expected to die. God delivered them, and the Corinthians helped by prayer. Paul then explains why he changed his travel plan. He was not saying yes and no, for God’s promises are yes in Christ. He stayed away to spare them.

verse.text: We don’t control your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy. For you stand firm in faith.

2-corinthians-11.summary: Paul asks them to bear with a little foolishness. He fears they will be led astray, as the serpent deceived Eve. He taught them free of charge, and other assemblies supported him. He calls his rivals false apostles. Then he boasts as a fool. He lists labors, prisons, beatings, shipwrecks, dangers, hunger, and cold. Besides these he carries daily concern for all the assemblies. He ends with his escape from Damascus in a basket through the wall.

verse.text: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that concern my weakness.

galatians-1.summary: Paul writes to the assemblies of Galatia as an apostle sent by Jesus Christ. He gives no thanks. He is amazed that they are turning so quickly to a different good news. He says anyone who brings another message is cursed. His message did not come from a human source. He once persecuted the assembly and advanced in Judaism. God called him, and he went to Arabia, not to Jerusalem. After three years he visited Peter for fifteen days and saw James.

verse.text: For I didn’t receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but it came to me through revelation of Jesus Christ.

routes.title: From Damascus up to Jerusalem
routes.text: Paul says he went away into Arabia and returned to Damascus. After three years he went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter.
routes.note: The line joins the places Galatians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

galatians-2.summary: After fourteen years Paul goes to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus. Titus, a Greek, is not forced to be circumcised. James, Peter, and John give Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship. They ask only that he remember the poor. In Antioch Peter eats with Gentiles, then draws back when men come from James. Barnabas is carried along too. Paul rebukes Peter before everyone. He says a person is justified by faith in Christ, not by law.

verse.text: But when I saw that they didn’t walk uprightly according to the truth of the Good News, I said to Peter before them all, “If you, being a Jew, live as the Gentiles do, and not as the Jews do, why do you compel the Gentiles to live as the Jews do?

routes.title: Up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus
routes.text: After fourteen years Paul goes up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus. He lays his message before the leaders.
routes.note: The line joins the places Galatians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

galatians-4.summary: Paul says an heir who is a child is no different from a servant. God sent his Son, born of a woman, to redeem those under the law. Now they are sons and call God Abba, Father. He asks why they turn back to weak principles and observe days and seasons. He recalls how they welcomed him when he was ill. He is in labor again until Christ is formed in them. Then he tells of Abraham’s two sons, by Hagar and by the free woman. He says believers are children of the free woman.

verse.text: These things contain an allegory, for these are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children to bondage, which is Hagar.

ephesians-1.summary: The letter opens in Paul’s name to the saints at Ephesus. It blesses God for choosing them in Christ before the world’s foundation. In Christ they have redemption through his blood and forgiveness. God plans to sum up all things in Christ. They were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, a pledge of their inheritance. Paul has heard of their faith and love and gives thanks. He prays that they will know their hope and God’s power. That power raised Christ and made him head over all things.

verse.text: having the eyes of your hearts enlightened, that you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what are the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints,

philippians-1.summary: Paul and Timothy write to the saints at Philippi with their overseers and servants. Paul thanks God for their partnership from the first day. He prays that their love will grow in knowledge. He says his chains have helped the good news spread through the whole guard. Some announce Christ from envy, some from good will, and he rejoices. He does not know whether he will live or die. To live is Christ, and to die is gain. He asks them to stand firm in one spirit and not fear their opponents.

verse.text: Yet to remain in the flesh is more needful for your sake.

colossians-1.summary: Paul and Timothy write to the saints at Colossae. They thank God for the faith of readers whom Epaphras taught. They pray that the readers be filled with knowledge of God’s will. The Father moved them from darkness into the kingdom of his Son. A passage of praise follows. The Son is God’s image, and all things were created through him. He is head of the body, and through him God reconciles all things. Paul rejoices in his sufferings and labors to present everyone mature in Christ.

verse.text: and through him to reconcile all things to himself by him, whether things on the earth or things in the heavens, having made peace through the blood of his cross.

colossians-2.summary: Paul says he struggles for the readers and for those at Laodicea. All the treasures of wisdom are hidden in Christ. They should walk in him as they were taught. He warns against philosophy and empty deceit built on human tradition. In Christ all the fullness of deity lives in bodily form. God forgave them and nailed the record of debt to the cross. No one should judge them about food, festivals, new moons, or Sabbaths. Rules like “Don’t handle, nor taste, nor touch” have no value against the flesh.

verse.text: and not holding firmly to the Head, from whom all the body, being supplied and knit together through the joints and ligaments, grows with God’s growth.

colossians-4.summary: Masters are told to give their servants what is just and equal. Paul asks for prayer that a door will open for the word. He is in chains for it. He sends Tychicus and Onesimus to report his news. Aristarchus, Mark, Jesus called Justus, Epaphras, Luke, and Demas send greetings. He greets the brothers in Laodicea and the assembly in the house of Nymphas. The letter is to be read in Laodicea too. Paul signs with his own hand and asks them to remember his chains.

verse.text: When this letter has been read among you, cause it to be read also in the assembly of the Laodiceans, and that you also read the letter from Laodicea.

1-thessalonians-1.summary: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write to the assembly of the Thessalonians. They thank God for the readers’ faith, love, and enduring hope. The good news came to them in power and in the Holy Spirit. They received the word in much affliction with joy. They became an example to believers in Macedonia and Achaia. People everywhere tell how they turned from idols to serve the living God. They wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised.

verse.text: You became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit,

1-thessalonians-2.summary: Paul recalls that they came to Thessalonica after being mistreated at Philippi. They did not use flattery or seek glory or money. They were gentle, like a nursing mother with her children. They worked night and day so as not to burden anyone. They urged each one as a father does. The readers accepted the message as God’s word and suffered from their own countrymen. Paul speaks sharply of those in Judea who opposed the assemblies there. He wanted to return, but Satan hindered him, and the readers are his joy.

verse.text: Even so, affectionately longing for you, we were well pleased to impart to you not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.

1-thessalonians-3.summary: Paul could not bear the separation and sent Timothy from Athens. Timothy was to strengthen them so that no one would be shaken by afflictions. Paul had warned them that suffering would come. He feared the tempter had tempted them and the work was wasted. Timothy has now returned with good news of their faith and love. Paul says he lives if they stand firm in the Lord. He prays night and day to see them and supply what their faith lacks. He prays that their love will increase.

verse.text: But Timothy has just now come to us from you, and brought us glad news of your faith and love, and that you have good memories of us always, longing to see us, even as we also long to see you.

routes.title: Timothy is sent from Athens
routes.text: Paul stays behind at Athens and sends Timothy to strengthen the Thessalonians. Timothy comes back with good news of their faith.
routes.note: The line joins the places 1 Thessalonians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

2-thessalonians-1.summary: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write again to the Thessalonians. They thank God that the readers’ faith grows and their love increases. They boast of the readers’ endurance in persecutions. They say God will repay the afflicters and give relief to the afflicted. That will happen when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his angels. Those who do not obey the good news will be punished. He will be glorified in his saints on that day. The writers pray that God will count the readers worthy of their calling.

verse.text: To this end we also pray always for you that our God may count you worthy of your calling, and fulfill every desire of goodness and work of faith with power,

1-timothy-1.summary: The letter is addressed from Paul to Timothy, his true child in faith. Timothy is to stay in Ephesus and stop certain people from teaching different doctrine. They occupy themselves with myths and endless lists of ancestors. The law is good when used lawfully, against the lawless. Paul thanks Christ, who put him in service though he was a persecutor. Christ Jesus came to save sinners, and Paul calls himself the chief. Timothy is to fight the good fight with faith and a good conscience. Hymenaeus and Alexander have wrecked their faith.

verse.text: But the goal of this command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith,

2-timothy-1.summary: The letter is addressed from Paul to Timothy, his beloved child. Paul remembers Timothy’s tears and longs to see him. He recalls the faith of Timothy’s grandmother Lois and mother Eunice. Timothy is to stir up God’s gift, given through Paul’s hands. God gave a spirit of power, love, and self-control, not fear. Timothy should not be ashamed of the Lord or of Paul the prisoner. All in Asia turned away from Paul. Onesiphorus was not ashamed of his chain and searched for him in Rome.

verse.text: Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but endure hardship for the Good News according to the power of God,

2-timothy-4.summary: Paul charges Timothy before God and Christ, the judge of living and dead. Timothy is to announce the word and be ready at all times. A time will come when people gather teachers who please their ears. Paul says he is already being poured out. He has fought the good fight and kept the faith. He asks Timothy to come soon and bring Mark, a cloak, and the books. At his first defense no one stood with him, but the Lord did. He sends greetings and a blessing.

verse.text: preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and exhort with all patience and teaching.

titus-1.summary: The letter is addressed from Paul to Titus, his true child in faith. Paul left Titus in Crete to appoint elders in every city. An elder must be blameless, the husband of one wife, with believing children. An overseer must not be self-pleasing, quick to anger, violent, or greedy. He must be hospitable, self-controlled, and hold to the faithful word. Many unruly talkers upset whole households for dishonest gain. The letter quotes a Cretan saying against Cretans. Titus is to rebuke them sharply.

verse.text: holding to the faithful word which is according to the teaching, that he may be able to exhort in the sound doctrine, and to convict those who contradict him.

revelation-1.summary: The book calls itself a revelation of Jesus Christ, sent to John. John writes to seven assemblies in Asia. He was on the island of Patmos because of God’s word. On the Lord’s day he hears a voice like a trumpet. He sees one like a son of man among seven golden lampstands. His eyes are like fire, and a sharp sword comes from his mouth. John falls at his feet like a dead man. The figure tells him to write, and says the lampstands are the seven assemblies.

verse.text: and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever. Amen. I have the keys of Death and of Hades.

routes.title: The book goes to seven assemblies
routes.intro: John, the apostle, has been banished to the island of Patmos for his testimony of Jesus. The seven assemblies are churches in the Roman province of Asia.
routes.text: John is on the island of Patmos. A voice tells him to write what he sees and send it to seven assemblies.
routes.note: The line joins the places Revelation names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

revelation-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

revelation-2.summary: John writes four messages from Christ. Ephesus has worked hard and tested false apostles but has left its first love. Smyrna is poor and yet rich, and will suffer for ten days. Pergamum holds fast where Satan’s throne is, yet some hold the teaching of Balaam. Thyatira has love and service but tolerates a woman called Jezebel. Each message ends with a promise to the one who overcomes. Each tells those with ears to hear what the Spirit says.

verse.text: Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and do the first works; or else I am coming to you swiftly, and will move your lamp stand out of its place, unless you repent.

revelation-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

revelation-3.summary: John writes three more messages. Sardis has a name for being alive and is dead. A few there have not soiled their clothes. Philadelphia has little power, has kept Christ’s word, and has an open door. Laodicea is neither cold nor hot and will be spat out. It says it is rich, yet it is poor, blind, and naked. Christ counsels it to buy gold, white clothes, and eye salve from him. He stands at the door and knocks.

verse.text: As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent.

revelation-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

gabriel-comes-to-mary.summary: An angel tells the old priest Zacharias that his wife Elizabeth will bear a son. Zacharias doubts and cannot speak. The angel Gabriel comes to Mary. Her son will be called the Son of the Most High. Mary visits Elizabeth, who blesses her. Mary sings that God has looked on her low position. John is born, and Zacharias speaks again and praises God.

verse.text: Behold, you will conceive in your womb and give birth to a son, and shall name him ‘Jesus.’

alsoRead.note: Nephi sees the virgin who will be the mother of the Son of God.
Alma says the Son of God will be born of Mary.

jesus-is-born.summary: In Matthew, an angel tells Joseph in a dream to marry Mary. Caesar Augustus orders a count of the people, and Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem. Mary gives birth and lays her son in a manger, a feeding trough. Angels announce the birth to shepherds in the fields. In the temple, old Simeon calls the child a light for the nations. The prophetess Anna gives thanks. At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the temple among the teachers.

verse.text: For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.

alsoRead.note: The Lord tells Nephi he will come into the world the next day.

routes.title: Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem
routes.text: Joseph goes up from Nazareth to Bethlehem to be enrolled. Mary goes with him.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: To the temple and home
routes.text: They bring the child to Jerusalem to present him. Then they return to Nazareth.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The Passover trip at age twelve
routes.text: His parents go up to Jerusalem for the Passover. The boy stays behind in the temple, then goes home with them.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

the-wise-men.summary: Wise men from the east come to Jerusalem seeking the newborn king of the Jews. King Herod is troubled. The star leads the wise men to the child, and they worship him with gifts. A dream warns them not to return to Herod. An angel tells Joseph to flee to Egypt with the child and his mother. Herod kills the young boys of Bethlehem. After Herod dies, the family settles in Nazareth.

verse.text: They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

routes.title: The wise men go to Bethlehem
routes.text: Wise men from the east ask in Jerusalem for the newborn king. Herod sends them on to Bethlehem.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Flight into Egypt
routes.text: An angel warns Joseph in a dream. He takes the child and his mother to Egypt by night.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Return to Nazareth
routes.text: After Herod dies, Joseph brings the family back. He fears Archelaus in Judea and settles in Nazareth.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

jesus-is-baptized.summary: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judea. He tells people to repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near. Crowds come and are baptized in the Jordan. Luke adds that John tells them to share their coats and food. John says one mightier than he is coming. Jesus comes to be baptized. The Spirit comes down like a dove, and a voice calls him God's beloved Son.

verse.text: Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”

alsoRead.note: Nephi asks how much more we need baptism, if the Lamb was baptized.

routes.title: Jesus comes to the Jordan
routes.text: Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan, and John baptizes him.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

jesus-begins-in-galilee.summary: The Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness, where he fasts forty days. He answers each temptation of the devil from Scripture. In Nazareth he reads from Isaiah and says it is fulfilled that day. His hometown tries to throw him off a cliff. He calls the fishermen Simon, Andrew, James, and John, and they leave their nets. He teaches in Capernaum and heals many. He calls Levi, a tax collector, to follow him.

verse.text: He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”

routes.title: Jesus moves to Capernaum
routes.text: Jesus hears that John is in prison. He leaves Nazareth and lives in Capernaum by the sea.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From Nazareth to the Jordan and Capernaum
routes.text: Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptized in the Jordan. He then goes into Galilee and enters Capernaum.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From the Jordan to Nazareth and Capernaum
routes.text: Jesus returns from the Jordan and is tested in the wilderness. He reads in Nazareth and then goes down to Capernaum.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

sermon-on-the-mount.summary: Jesus goes up a mountain and teaches his disciples. He calls the poor in spirit, the mourners, and the merciful blessed. His followers are salt and light. He has come to fulfill the law, not to destroy it. He tells them to love their enemies and pray for those who hurt them. Luke tells a similar sermon on a level place. There Jesus also chooses twelve apostles.

verse.text: Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

alsoRead.note: The risen Jesus gives a like sermon to the Nephites.

faith-in-capernaum.summary: A Roman officer asks Jesus to heal his servant. He says Jesus need only speak the word, and Jesus marvels at his faith. Four men lower a paralyzed man through a roof, and Jesus forgives and heals him. Jesus eats with tax collectors and sinners. He says the Sabbath was made for people. Luke adds that Jesus raises a widow's son at Nain. A woman weeps over his feet, and he forgives her sins.

verse.text: When Jesus heard it, he marveled and said to those who followed, “Most certainly I tell you, I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel.

the-twelve-are-chosen.summary: In a synagogue, Jesus sees a man with a withered hand. His opponents watch to see if he will heal on the Sabbath. He asks if the Sabbath is for saving life or killing. They say nothing, and he heals the man. The Pharisees begin to plot his death. Jesus appoints twelve to be with him and to preach. He says those who do God's will are his family.

verse.text: He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good or to do harm? To save a life or to kill?” But they were silent.

parables-and-the-storm.summary: Jesus teaches a large crowd from a boat. A farmer sows seed on the path, on rock, among thorns, and on good soil. The kingdom is like a tiny mustard seed that grows large. Luke adds that women travel with Jesus and support him from their own goods. That evening a storm fills the boat while Jesus sleeps. He rebukes the wind, and the sea is calm. The disciples ask who this is.

verse.text: He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm.

jairus-daughter.summary: Jesus crosses the lake and frees a man held by many demons. The townspeople beg Jesus to leave. Jairus, a synagogue leader, begs him to come to his dying daughter. On the way a woman who has bled for twelve years touches his cloak. She is healed, and Jesus stops to find her. Word comes that the girl has died. Jesus takes her hand, and she gets up.

verse.text: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”

feeding-the-five-thousand.summary: Herod has John the Baptist beheaded. A crowd follows Jesus to a quiet place. He feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish. That night he walks on the sea toward the disciples' boat. John adds that the crowd wants to make him king. Jesus says he is the bread of life that came down from heaven. Many disciples call this hard and leave. Peter says there is no one else to go to.

verse.text: Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.

johns-question.summary: John the Baptist is in prison and hears what Jesus is doing. He sends disciples to ask if Jesus is the one to come. Jesus tells them to report what they see and hear. He praises John as more than a prophet. He rebukes towns that saw his works and did not repent. He invites the weary to come to him and find rest.

verse.text: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

the-canaanite-womans-faith.summary: Pharisees ask why the disciples do not wash their hands before eating. Jesus says they set aside God's command for their own tradition. What comes out of the mouth defiles a person, not what goes in. He travels to the region of Tyre and Sidon. A Canaanite woman begs him to heal her daughter. She keeps asking, and he praises her faith and heals the girl. Mark adds that he heals a deaf man.

verse.text: Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Be it done to you even as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.

routes.title: Jesus withdraws toward Tyre and Sidon
routes.text: Jesus withdraws into the region of Tyre and Sidon. A Canaanite woman meets him there.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Through Tyre and Sidon to the lake
routes.text: Jesus goes to the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He comes back to the Sea of Galilee through the Decapolis.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

peters-confession.summary: Jesus asks his disciples who they say he is. Peter answers that he is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus blesses him and speaks of building his church. Then he says he must suffer, be killed, and rise. Peter rebukes him, and Jesus rebukes Peter. Anyone who follows him must take up a cross. Luke adds that Jesus sets his face to go to Jerusalem.

verse.text: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

routes.title: Jesus goes toward Caesarea Philippi
routes.text: Jesus comes into the parts of Caesarea Philippi. He asks the disciples who people say he is.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From Bethsaida toward Caesarea Philippi
routes.text: Jesus heals a blind man at Bethsaida. He then goes to the villages of Caesarea Philippi.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Jesus sets out for Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus sets his face to go to Jerusalem. The following chapters stay on this journey.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

the-transfiguration.summary: Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. His face shines like the sun, and Moses and Elijah appear with him. A bright cloud covers them, and a voice calls Jesus the beloved Son. Below, a father asks Jesus to heal his son. The father cries that he believes and asks help for his unbelief. Jesus heals the boy. He again says he will be killed and raised.

verse.text: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. Behold, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”

alsoRead.note: The Lord speaks of what the three saw on the mount.

the-good-samaritan.summary: Jesus sends seventy others ahead of him in pairs. A lawyer asks what he must do to inherit eternal life. He agrees that the law says to love God and neighbor. Then he asks who his neighbor is. Jesus tells of a man beaten by robbers on the road to Jericho. A priest and a Levite pass by. A Samaritan stops and cares for him. Jesus then visits Martha and Mary.

verse.text: He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”

routes.title: The road in the parable
routes.intro: A lawyer asks Jesus who his neighbor is. Jesus answers with the parable of the good Samaritan.
routes.text: A man goes down from Jerusalem to Jericho and falls among robbers.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

a-bent-woman-healed.summary: People tell Jesus about Galileans whom Pilate killed. He asks if they were worse sinners than others, and says no. He says everyone must repent. He tells of a fig tree given one more year to bear fruit. On a Sabbath he heals a woman bent over for eighteen years. The synagogue ruler objects. Jesus grieves over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets.

verse.text: When Jesus saw her, he called her and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”

ten-lepers.summary: Jesus tells his disciples to forgive. Between Samaria and Galilee, ten men with leprosy, a skin disease, cry out for mercy. Jesus tells them to show themselves to the priests. They are healed as they go. One returns, praises God, and thanks Jesus. He is a Samaritan. The Pharisees ask when God's kingdom will come.

verse.text: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.

the-pharisee-and-the-tax-collector.summary: Jesus tells of a widow who keeps asking an unjust judge for justice. He tells of two men who pray in the temple. A Pharisee thanks God that he is not like other people. A tax collector asks only for mercy. Jesus welcomes infants brought to him. A rich ruler asks about eternal life and leaves sad. Near Jericho, Jesus gives sight to a blind beggar.

verse.text: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’

the-rich-young-man.summary: Jesus teaches about marriage and blesses the children. A rich young man asks what he must do for eternal life. Jesus tells him to sell what he has and give to the poor. The young man goes away sad. Jesus tells of workers who all get the same wage, however long they worked. James and John ask for the best seats in his kingdom. Jesus says the great must be servants. At Jericho, the blind Bartimaeus receives his sight.

verse.text: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

routes.title: Jesus leaves Galilee
routes.text: Jesus departs from Galilee. He comes into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Up from Jericho toward Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus goes up toward Jerusalem with the twelve. A great crowd follows him out of Jericho.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Beyond the Jordan to Jericho
routes.text: Jesus teaches beyond the Jordan, then goes up toward Jerusalem. He heals Bartimaeus as he leaves Jericho.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

first-disciples.summary: John's Gospel opens with the Word, who was with God and was God. The Word became flesh and lived among us. John the Baptist says he is not the Christ. He points to Jesus as the Lamb of God. Two of John's disciples follow Jesus. Andrew brings his brother Simon. Philip brings Nathanael.

verse.text: The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

routes.title: From the Jordan to Galilee
routes.text: John baptizes at Bethany beyond the Jordan. The next day Jesus decides to go into Galilee.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

wedding-at-cana.summary: Jesus and his disciples go to a wedding at Cana. The wine runs out, and his mother tells him. He has six stone jars filled with water. The water becomes fine wine, and his disciples believe in him. At Passover he drives the sellers and money changers out of the temple. He says he will raise this temple in three days. He was speaking of his body.

verse.text: This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.

routes.title: From Cana to Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus is at a wedding in Cana. He goes down to Capernaum and then up to Jerusalem for the Passover.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

nicodemus.summary: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler, comes to Jesus at night. Jesus says no one can see God's kingdom without being born again. Nicodemus asks how that can be. Jesus says God so loved the world that he gave his only Son. Light has come, and people loved darkness. John the Baptist says Jesus must increase and he must decrease.

verse.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

woman-at-the-well.summary: Jesus travels through Samaria and rests at Jacob's well. He asks a Samaritan woman for a drink. He offers her living water and tells her about her life. She asks where people ought to worship. He says true worshipers worship in spirit and truth. She tells her town to come and see. Many Samaritans believe. In Galilee he heals an official's son with a word.

verse.text: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”

routes.title: Through Samaria to Galilee
routes.text: Jesus leaves Judea and passes through Samaria. He stops at Sychar and comes again to Cana. Jerusalem stands for Judea here.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

pool-of-bethesda.summary: In Jerusalem many sick people lie beside a pool. One man has been ill for thirty-eight years. Jesus asks if he wants to be well. The man says he has no one to put him in the water. Jesus tells him to take up his mat and walk. It is the Sabbath, and the leaders object. Jesus says his Father is working, and so is he.

verse.text: Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.”

routes.title: Up to Jerusalem for a feast
routes.text: Jesus goes up to Jerusalem for a feast of the Jews.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

light-of-the-world.summary: Jesus goes up to the Feast of Booths and teaches in the temple. The crowd is divided over him. On the last day he invites the thirsty to come and drink. Officers sent to arrest him return and say no one ever spoke like this. He says he is the light of the world. He tells them the truth will set them free. He says that before Abraham was, he is.

verse.text: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”

routes.title: Up to the feast in secret
routes.text: Jesus stays in Galilee while his brothers go up. Then he goes up to the feast in secret.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

man-born-blind.summary: Jesus sees a man blind from birth. The disciples ask whose sin caused it. Jesus says neither, and he heals the man with mud and washing. The Pharisees question the man again and again. His parents are afraid and say he can speak for himself. He says he was blind and now sees. They throw him out, and Jesus finds him.

verse.text: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”

the-good-shepherd.summary: Jesus says the sheep know the shepherd's voice. A thief comes only to steal and kill. Jesus says he is the door and the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. He has other sheep that are not of this fold. He says he and the Father are one, and some pick up stones.

verse.text: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

alsoRead.note: Jesus tells the Nephites they are the other sheep.

routes.title: Jesus goes beyond the Jordan
routes.text: Jesus goes away beyond the Jordan to the place where John first baptized.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

lazarus-raised.summary: Lazarus of Bethany falls ill, and his sisters send for Jesus. Jesus arrives after Lazarus has been dead four days. Martha says she believes he is the Christ. Jesus weeps at the tomb. He calls Lazarus out, and the dead man comes out wrapped in cloths. The council fears what Rome will do. The high priest says one man should die for the people.

verse.text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.

routes.title: Jesus comes to Bethany
routes.text: Jesus waits two days after he hears Lazarus is sick. Then he goes to Bethany, near Jerusalem.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

jesus-enters-jerusalem.summary: In Jericho, Zacchaeus the tax collector climbs a tree to see Jesus. He promises to repay those he cheated. At Bethany, Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly perfume. Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey, and crowds praise him. Luke says he weeps over the city. He drives the traders out of the temple. The leaders want to arrest him but fear the crowds.

verse.text: The multitudes who went in front of him, and those who followed, kept shouting, “Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”

routes.title: Jesus enters Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus rides down from the Mount of Olives into Jerusalem. That evening he goes out to Bethany.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Jesus enters Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus rides from the Mount of Olives into Jerusalem. He looks around the temple and goes out to Bethany.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From Jericho up to Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus passes through Jericho and meets Zacchaeus. He goes up by Bethany and the Mount of Olives and weeps over the city.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From Bethany into Jerusalem
routes.text: Jesus comes to Bethany six days before the Passover. The next day a crowd meets him as he comes to Jerusalem.
routes.note: The line joins the places John names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

jesus-enters-jerusalem.dateDetail: Years from Matthew 21; Mark 11; Luke 19; John 12.

teaching-in-the-temple.summary: Jesus tells of tenants who kill a vineyard owner's son. He is asked about paying taxes to Caesar and about the resurrection. A scribe asks which commandment is first. Jesus names love of God and love of neighbor. Matthew adds his woes on the scribes and Pharisees, who neglect justice and mercy. He watches people give at the temple treasury. A poor widow gives two small coins, all she has.

verse.text: He called his disciples to himself and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,

signs-of-his-coming.summary: Jesus says the temple's stones will all be thrown down. On the Mount of Olives his disciples ask when this will happen. He warns of false christs, wars, famines, and persecution. Jerusalem will be surrounded by armies. The Son of Man will come in the clouds. No one knows the day or the hour. So they must watch and be ready.

verse.text: “But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

last-supper-and-gethsemane.summary: Judas agrees to hand Jesus over for thirty pieces of silver. Jesus eats the Passover with the Twelve and gives them the bread and the cup. In Gethsemane he prays in anguish while the disciples sleep. Judas comes with an armed crowd, and Jesus is arrested. The council condemns him. Peter denies him three times. John adds that Pilate asks if Jesus is a king.

verse.text: saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”

alsoRead.note: King Benjamin says blood will come from every pore.
The Lord describes his suffering in his own words.

routes.title: From Bethany to the Mount of Olives
routes.text: Jesus is at Bethany, then keeps the Passover in the city. After the hymn they go out to the Mount of Olives.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From Bethany to the Mount of Olives
routes.text: A woman anoints Jesus at Bethany. He keeps the Passover in the city and goes out to the Mount of Olives.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

last-supper-and-gethsemane.dateDetail: Years from Matthew 26; Mark 14; Luke 22; John 18.

the-crucifixion.summary: Pilate says he finds no guilt in Jesus. The crowd asks for Barabbas instead. Pilate hands Jesus over to be crucified. Soldiers mock him with a crown of thorns. He is crucified between two robbers. Luke says he prays for those who crucify him. He says, “It is finished,” and dies. Joseph of Arimathea buries him in a tomb.

verse.text: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, “It is finished!” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

alsoRead.note: In the Americas a great storm arises.

the-crucifixion.dateDetail: Years from Matthew 27; Mark 15; Luke 23; John 19.

the-resurrection.summary: At dawn after the Sabbath, women come to the tomb and find it empty. Angels say Jesus has risen. Mary Magdalene meets Jesus and knows him when he says her name. Two disciples walk with him to Emmaus and know him when he breaks bread. He appears to the disciples behind locked doors. Thomas touches his wounds and believes. Jesus sends them to teach all nations.

verse.text: He isn’t here, but is risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee,

alsoRead.note: The risen Jesus shows himself to the Nephites.

routes.title: The eleven go to Galilee
routes.text: The angel says the risen Jesus goes ahead into Galilee. The eleven go to the mountain there.
routes.note: The line joins the places Matthew names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The message points to Galilee
routes.text: The young man at the tomb says Jesus goes ahead into Galilee. The disciples will see him there.
routes.note: The line joins the places Mark names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Jesus leads them out to Bethany
routes.text: Jesus leads the disciples out as far as Bethany and blesses them.
routes.note: The line joins the places Luke names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

the-resurrection.dateDetail: Years from Matthew 28; Mark 16; Luke 24; John 20.

feed-my-sheep.summary: Seven disciples fish all night on the Sea of Galilee and catch nothing. At dawn a man on the shore tells them to cast on the right side. The net fills, and they know it is the Lord. He gives them bread and fish beside a fire. He asks Peter three times if he loves him. Each time he tells Peter to feed his sheep.

verse.text: He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?” Peter was grieved because he asked him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.

jesus-ascends.summary: The risen Jesus teaches the apostles for forty days. He tells them to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Spirit. They will be his witnesses to the ends of the earth. He is taken up, and two men in white speak to them. About 120 believers pray together. They cast lots to choose a witness in place of Judas. The lot falls on Matthias.

verse.text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”

pentecost.summary: On the day of Pentecost, a sound like wind fills the house. Tongues like fire rest on the believers, and they speak in other languages. Jews from many nations hear them in their own languages. Peter says God raised Jesus from the dead. The hearers ask what they should do. Peter tells them to repent and be baptized. About three thousand join and share their goods.

verse.text: Peter said to them, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

peter-heals-a-lame-man.summary: A man lame from birth asks Peter and John for money at the temple gate. Peter says he has no silver or gold. He tells the man to walk in the name of Jesus Christ. The man leaps and praises God. The council arrests Peter and John and orders them not to speak of Jesus. They say they cannot stop telling what they saw. The believers pray for courage and share what they own.

verse.text: But Peter said, “I have no silver or gold, but what I have, that I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!”

ananias-and-sapphira.summary: Ananias and Sapphira sell land and keep part of the price. They bring the rest as if it were all of it. Peter says Ananias lied to God, and Ananias falls dead. Sapphira tells the same lie and also dies. An angel opens the jail where the apostles are held. Before the council Peter says they must obey God rather than men. The teacher Gamaliel advises caution, and the apostles are beaten and released.

verse.text: But Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than men.

stephen-is-stoned.summary: Greek-speaking widows are being missed in the daily food. The apostles ask the believers to choose seven men for this work. One of them is Stephen. Men from a synagogue bring false witnesses against him. Stephen answers with Israel's history. He says his hearers resist the Holy Spirit as their fathers did. They stone him, and he prays that the sin not be held against them.

verse.text: He kneeled down and cried with a loud voice, “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!” When he had said this, he fell asleep.

philip-and-the-ethiopian.summary: Saul approves of Stephen's death, and persecution scatters the believers. Philip teaches in Samaria, and many are baptized. Peter and John lay hands on them, and they receive the Holy Spirit. Simon, a sorcerer, offers money for that power, and Peter rebukes him. An angel sends Philip to a desert road. An Ethiopian official is reading Isaiah in his chariot. Philip tells him about Jesus and baptizes him.

verse.text: Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached to him about Jesus.

routes.title: Philip goes to Samaria
routes.intro: Stephen has been stoned in Jerusalem, and Saul is leading a persecution of the church. Philip was one of the seven chosen to serve the believers.
routes.text: Persecution scatters the Jerusalem assembly. Philip goes down to the city of Samaria and proclaims the Christ.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The road from Jerusalem to Gaza
routes.intro: Philip, one of the seven, has been preaching in Samaria. The Ethiopian official, treasurer to his queen, is going home from worship in Jerusalem.
routes.text: An angel sends Philip to this road. He meets the Ethiopian official on it. Acts does not say where.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Philip from Azotus to Caesarea
routes.intro: Philip has just baptized the Ethiopian official on the Gaza road. Then the Spirit takes him away.
routes.text: Philip is found at Azotus. He preaches in the towns until he reaches Caesarea.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

saul-on-the-damascus-road.summary: Saul travels to Damascus to arrest followers of Jesus. A light from the sky stops him, and a voice says it is Jesus. He is blind for three days. The Lord sends a disciple named Ananias to him. Ananias lays hands on Saul, and Saul sees and is baptized. Saul preaches Jesus, and some plot to kill him. Peter heals Aeneas and raises Tabitha in Joppa.

verse.text: But the Lord said to him, “Go your way, for he is my chosen vessel to bear my name before the nations and kings, and the children of Israel.

alsoRead.note: An angel also stops Alma and the sons of Mosiah.

routes.title: Saul sets out for Damascus
routes.intro: Saul, a Pharisee, is arresting followers of Jesus. He sets out to bring any he finds in Damascus back to Jerusalem in chains.
routes.text: Saul sets out for Damascus with letters from the high priest. A light stops him near the city.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Saul escapes to Tarsus
routes.intro: Saul, now a believer, has been preaching in Damascus that Jesus is the Son of God. The Jews there plot to kill him.
routes.text: Disciples lower Saul over the Damascus wall in a basket. He goes to Jerusalem. The brothers then send him to Tarsus by Caesarea.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Peter from Lydda to Joppa
routes.text: Peter heals Aeneas at Lydda. Two men bring him to Joppa, where Tabitha has died.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

peter-and-cornelius.summary: Cornelius is a Roman officer in Caesarea who fears God. An angel tells him to send for Peter. In Joppa, Peter sees a vision of a sheet full of animals. A voice tells him not to call unclean what God has made clean. In Cornelius' house the Holy Spirit falls on the Gentile hearers. Peter baptizes them. In Antioch the disciples are first called Christians.

verse.text: Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism;

routes.title: Cornelius sends for Peter
routes.intro: Cornelius is a Roman centurion at Caesarea, a Gentile who prays to God. An angel has told him to send for Peter.
routes.text: Cornelius sends two servants and a soldier to Joppa to fetch Peter.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Peter goes to Caesarea
routes.intro: In a vision God has taught Peter to call no one unclean. Messengers from Cornelius, a Gentile centurion, have come for him.
routes.text: Peter goes with them the next day. Some brothers from Joppa go too.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Barnabas is sent to Antioch
routes.text: The Jerusalem assembly hears that Greeks in Antioch believe. It sends Barnabas there.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Barnabas brings Saul from Tarsus
routes.text: Barnabas goes to Tarsus to look for Saul and brings him to Antioch.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Relief for Judea
routes.text: The disciples at Antioch send relief to the elders in Judea. Barnabas and Saul carry it. Jerusalem stands for Judea here.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

peter-freed-from-prison.summary: King Herod kills James, the brother of John, with the sword. He arrests Peter, and the believers pray for him. At night an angel wakes Peter, and his chains fall off. The iron gate opens by itself. Peter goes to the house of Mary, mother of John Mark. A servant named Rhoda hears his voice and runs in without opening the gate. Later Herod accepts praise as a god, and an angel strikes him.

verse.text: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Stand up quickly!” His chains fell off his hands.

pauls-first-mission.summary: The Holy Spirit tells the believers at Antioch to set apart Barnabas and Saul. Saul is also called Paul. On Cyprus the governor believes. In Antioch of Pisidia, Paul preaches in the synagogue. When some oppose him, he turns to the Gentiles. In Lystra, Paul heals a man who had never walked. The crowd calls them gods, and they say they are only men. Opponents stir up the crowd, and Paul is stoned but gets up.

verse.text: As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”

routes.title: From Antioch to Cyprus and Pisidia
routes.intro: The church at Antioch is told by the Holy Spirit to set apart Barnabas and Saul. This is Paul's first mission.
routes.text: Barnabas and Saul sail to Cyprus and cross the island. They sail to Perga and go up to Antioch of Pisidia. Driven out, they go to Iconium.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Flight to Lystra and Derbe
routes.text: Paul and Barnabas flee a plot at Iconium. Paul is stoned at Lystra, and they go on to Derbe.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Return to Antioch
routes.text: They go back through the same cities and appoint elders. They sail from Attalia to Antioch.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

jerusalem-council.summary: Some teach that Gentile believers must be circumcised to be saved. Paul and Barnabas go to Jerusalem about it. Peter says God gave the Gentiles the Spirit and made no distinction. James proposes four things for Gentile believers to avoid. The apostles and elders send a letter, and Antioch rejoices. Paul and Barnabas disagree over John Mark and part ways.

verse.text: But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are.”

routes.title: Up to Jerusalem about the dispute
routes.intro: Some teachers from Judea are telling Gentile converts in Antioch that they must be circumcised to be saved.
routes.text: Antioch sends Paul and Barnabas to the apostles and elders. They pass through Phoenicia and Samaria.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The letter goes to Antioch
routes.intro: The council at Jerusalem has decided that Gentile converts need not be circumcised. Its letter tells the churches so.
routes.text: Judas and Silas carry the council’s letter to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

paul-in-philippi.summary: A vision of a man from Macedonia calls Paul across the sea. In Philippi, Lydia, a seller of purple cloth, believes and hosts them. Paul orders a spirit out of a slave girl who told fortunes. Her owners lose their income and accuse Paul and Silas. The two are beaten and jailed. At midnight an earthquake opens the doors. The jailer and his household are baptized.

verse.text: They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”

routes.title: From Lystra to Philippi
routes.intro: Paul and Silas set out on a second mission to visit the churches founded on the first.
routes.text: Paul meets Timothy at Lystra. They pass through Phrygia and Galatia to Troas. After the vision they sail to Macedonia.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

paul-in-athens.summary: In Thessalonica, Paul reasons from the Scriptures for three Sabbaths. Some believe, and others start a riot. In Berea the hearers study the Scriptures every day. In Athens, Paul is troubled by the city's idols. Philosophers bring him to the hill called the Areopagus. He speaks of the God who made the world and needs nothing. Some mock, some want to hear more, and a few believe.

verse.text: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands.

routes.title: From Philippi to Athens
routes.intro: On Paul's second mission he and Silas preach in Macedonia. In each city, opponents stir up crowds against them.
routes.text: Paul and Silas go to Thessalonica, then to Beroea by night. Brothers take Paul to the sea and on to Athens.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

letters-to-the-thessalonians.summary: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write to the believers at Thessalonica. They thank God for the readers' faith, love, and hope. The readers turned from idols to serve the living God. Paul recalls working night and day so he would not be a burden. He sent Timothy from Athens to strengthen them. Timothy has brought back good news of their faith. A second letter praises their endurance in persecution.

verse.text: For they themselves report concerning us what kind of a reception we had from you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve a living and true God,

routes.title: Timothy is sent from Athens
routes.text: Paul stays behind at Athens and sends Timothy to strengthen the Thessalonians. Timothy comes back with good news of their faith.
routes.note: The line joins the places 1 Thessalonians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

paul-in-corinth.summary: In Corinth, Paul lives and works with Aquila and Priscilla, who make tents. He teaches in the synagogue each Sabbath. When opposed, he moves next door. Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believes. The Lord tells Paul in a vision not to be afraid. The governor Gallio refuses to judge a dispute about Jewish law. In Ephesus, Priscilla and Aquila teach Apollos more fully.

verse.text: The Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision, “Don’t be afraid, but speak and don’t be silent;

routes.title: Paul comes to Corinth
routes.intro: On his second mission Paul has preached in Macedonia and at Athens.
routes.text: Paul leaves Athens for Corinth and stays a year and six months.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From Corinth back to Antioch
routes.intro: Paul has spent a year and a half founding the church at Corinth. He heads home to Antioch, ending his second mission.
routes.text: Paul sails for Syria by Cenchreae and Ephesus. He lands at Caesarea, greets the assembly, and goes down to Antioch.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

paul-in-ephesus.summary: In Ephesus, Paul baptizes twelve disciples, and they receive the Holy Spirit. He teaches there for two years. Many burn their books of magic. Demetrius, who makes silver shrines of the goddess Artemis, starts a riot. In Troas, young Eutychus falls from a window and is brought in alive. At Miletus, Paul calls the elders of Ephesus. He warns them to guard the flock, and they kneel and weep.

verse.text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”

routes.title: From Philippi to Miletus
routes.intro: Paul is ending his third mission. He is hurrying to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost with a gift for the poor saints there.
routes.text: The group sails from Philippi to Troas. Paul goes to Assos by land. The ship then passes the islands to Miletus.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

letters-to-the-corinthians.summary: Paul writes to the believers at Corinth, who are quarreling. Some follow Paul, and others Apollos or Peter. He says he preaches Christ crucified. Christ died for sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day. Some say there is no resurrection, and Paul answers them. The body is sown like a seed and raised imperishable. In a second letter he lists his beatings, shipwrecks, and dangers.

verse.text: But now Christ has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruit of those who are asleep.

alsoRead.note: Joseph Smith cites Paul on baptism for the dead.

routes.title: Paul’s plan to come to Corinth
routes.text: Paul will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost. Then he will pass through Macedonia and come to Corinth.
routes.note: The line joins the places 1 Corinthians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: The gift for Jerusalem
routes.text: Paul will send approved people with letters to carry the gift to Jerusalem. He may go with them.
routes.note: The line joins the places 1 Corinthians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

letter-to-the-galatians.summary: Paul writes to the believers of Galatia, who are turning to a different message. He says his message came from Jesus Christ, not from people. He once persecuted the church. In Jerusalem, James, Peter, and John give him the right hand of fellowship. In Antioch, Paul rebukes Peter for drawing back from Gentile believers. He says a person is made right with God by faith in Christ. Believers are God's children and heirs.

verse.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.

routes.title: From Damascus up to Jerusalem
routes.text: Paul says he went away into Arabia and returned to Damascus. After three years he went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter.
routes.note: The line joins the places Galatians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus
routes.text: After fourteen years Paul goes up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus. He lays his message before the leaders.
routes.note: The line joins the places Galatians names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

letter-to-the-romans.summary: Paul writes to the believers in Rome before he has visited them. He says he is not ashamed of the good news. It is God's power to save everyone who believes. He tells them to accept one another as Christ accepted them. He plans to visit Rome on his way to Spain. First he will carry a gift to the poor in Jerusalem.

verse.text: For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.

routes.title: Paul’s plan: Jerusalem, then Rome
routes.text: Paul says he is going to Jerusalem with a gift for the saints. After that he plans to visit Rome on the way to Spain.
routes.note: The line joins the places Romans names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

paul-arrested-in-jerusalem.summary: The prophet Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul's belt. He says Paul will be bound in Jerusalem. In the temple, men from Asia stir up the crowd, and Roman soldiers take Paul. Paul tells the crowd how he saw Jesus near Damascus. He says he is a Roman citizen, and they do not flog him. The Lord tells him he must testify in Rome. Soldiers take him by night to Caesarea.

verse.text: The following night, the Lord stood by him and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”

routes.title: From Miletus to Jerusalem
routes.intro: Paul is ending his third mission and going to Jerusalem with a gift for the poor saints, though he has been warned that chains await him.
routes.text: The ship passes Cos and Rhodes to Patara. A second ship crosses to Tyre. The group goes on by Ptolemais and Caesarea to Jerusalem.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: Paul is taken to Caesarea
routes.intro: Paul was arrested at the temple in Jerusalem. More than forty men have sworn to kill him, so the Roman commander sends him to the governor, Felix.
routes.text: Soldiers take Paul to Antipatris by night. Horsemen bring him on to the governor at Caesarea.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

paul-before-agrippa.summary: The high priest brings charges against Paul before the governor Felix. Paul says he worships the God of his fathers and hopes for a resurrection. Felix keeps him in prison for two years. When Festus becomes governor, Paul appeals to Caesar. Paul tells King Agrippa how he saw the light on the Damascus road. Festus says learning has made him mad. Agrippa says Paul could have gone free.

verse.text: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”

shipwreck-and-rome.summary: Paul sails for Italy as a prisoner. A violent storm drives the ship for many days. Paul says an angel told him no one will die. The ship breaks up, and all 276 people reach land on Malta. A viper bites Paul, and he is not harmed. In Rome he lives under guard for two years. He teaches all who come to him.

verse.text: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

routes.title: The voyage toward Italy
routes.intro: Paul is a prisoner. He has appealed to Caesar, so the governor, Festus, sends him to Rome under a centurion named Julius. Luke and Aristarchus sail with him, and at Myra they board a ship of Alexandria bound for Italy.
routes.text: The ship touches at Sidon and reaches Myra. A second ship leaves Fair Havens, and a storm drives it to Malta.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

routes.title: From Malta to Rome
routes.intro: Paul, a prisoner bound for trial before Caesar, was shipwrecked on Malta with everyone aboard. After three months the party sails on in another ship of Alexandria.
routes.text: Paul sails by Syracuse and Rhegium to Puteoli. Brothers meet him at the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns. This guide has no checked point for the Market of Appius.
routes.note: The line joins the places Acts names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.

letters-from-prison.summary: Paul writes letters while he is in chains. To the Colossians he says all things were created through the Son. He warns them against empty philosophy and human rules. To the Ephesians he blesses God for choosing them in Christ. He tells the Philippians that his chains have helped the good news spread. He does not know if he will live or die. To live is Christ, and to die is gain.

verse.text: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

letters-to-timothy-and-titus.summary: Paul writes to Timothy, who leads the believers at Ephesus. He tells Timothy to stop false teaching. He calls himself the chief of sinners whom Christ came to save. He writes to Titus, whom he left in Crete to appoint elders. In a last letter Paul says God gave a spirit of power, not fear. He says he has fought the good fight and kept the faith. He asks Timothy to come soon.

verse.text: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.

letters-to-the-seven-churches.summary: John is on the island of Patmos. On the Lord's day he sees one like a son of man among seven lampstands. The lampstands are seven churches in Asia. Christ sends a message to each one. Ephesus has left its first love, and Smyrna will suffer. Laodicea is neither cold nor hot. Christ stands at the door and knocks.

verse.text: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.

routes.title: The book goes to seven assemblies
routes.intro: John, the apostle, has been banished to the island of Patmos for his testimony of Jesus. The seven assemblies are churches in the Roman province of Asia.
routes.text: John is on the island of Patmos. A voice tells him to write what he sees and send it to seven assemblies.
routes.note: The line joins the places Revelation names, in order. It does not trace a road or a sea lane.
